180	      \"commit\": \"\"
181	    }
182	  }]" "$VENDOR_YAML"
183	  if [[ -n "$opt_series" ]]; then
184	    yq -i ".skills[-1].series = \"$opt_series\"" "$VENDOR_YAML"
185	  fi
186	  echo -e "${GREEN}done${NC}"
187	
188	  if [[ "$opt_sync" == "true" ]]; then
189	    echo ""
190	    "$SYNC_SCRIPT" "$name"
191	  else
192	    echo -e "\nRun ${YELLOW}make sync${NC} or ${YELLOW}./scripts/sync-vendor.sh $name${NC} to download the skill."
193	  fi
194	}
195	
196	main "$@"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# pre-push — run the catalog gates before anything leaves this machine.
3	#
4	# Installed by `make install-hooks` (symlinked to .git/hooks/pre-push).
5	# Mirrors .github/workflows/validate.yml, so CI failures show up here first.
6	#
7	# Bypass for a genuinely urgent push:  git push --no-verify
8	# Uninstall:                           rm .git/hooks/pre-push
9	
10	set -uo pipefail
11	
12	REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" || exit 1
13	cd "$REPO_ROOT" || exit 1
14	
15	LOG="$(mktemp -t agent-skills-prepush.XXXXXX)"
16	trap 'rm -f "$LOG"' EXIT
17	
18	printf 'pre-push: running make validate…\n' >&2
19	if make validate --no-print-directory >"$LOG" 2>&1; then
20	  printf 'pre-push: ok\n' >&2
21	  exit 0
22	fi
23	
24	printf '\npre-push: FAILED — push aborted:\n\n' >&2
25	tail -n 25 "$LOG" >&2
26	printf '\nRe-run in full with:  make validate\n(bypass with:         git push --no-verify)\n' >&2
27	exit 1

```text
1	# Creating local skills
2	
3	A local skill is a custom-authored skill maintained in this repo under
4	[`skills/local/<skill-name>/`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local).
5	
6	## Scaffold a new skill
7	
8	Use the bundled scaffolder (recommended — seeds the full agentskills.io
9	best-practice layout and fans out the discovery symlinks for non-universal
10	agents):
11	
12	```bash
13	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
14	```
15	
16	The script picks one of three **placement scopes** by walking up from your
17	CWD; override with `--local` / `--project` / `--global` when intent isn't
18	obvious:
19	
20	| Scope | Trigger | Canonical dir | Symlinks created |
21	|---|---|---|---|
22	| **LOCAL** | `vendor.yaml` / `skills/local/` / `skills/.claude-plugin/` found | `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/` with `--vendor`) | `.agents/skills/<name>` + `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>` |
23	| **PROJECT** | `.git` found | `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents — Cursor/Codex/OpenCode/Warp — pick this up directly) | `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any non-universal agent dir already present at the repo root) |
24	| **GLOBAL** | neither anchor, or `--global` | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `~/.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any non-universal agent dir already present under `$HOME`) |
25	
26	This mirrors the placement contract of `npx skills add` (canonical content
27	in `.agents/skills/` + relative symlinks into each non-universal agent's
28	home), so a skill scaffolded here will be picked up by Claude Code,
29	Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Warp, etc. without any extra wiring. See
30	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](../reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
31	for the upstream mechanism.
32	
33	Alternative (just the SKILL.md skeleton, no symlinks, no `references/` /
34	`scripts/` / `assets/`):
35	
36	```bash
37	cd skills/local
38	npx skills@latest init [skill-name]
39	```
40	
41	This creates only `skills/local/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` with the required
42	YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`).
43	
44	Before writing the description, check the repo's
45	[Agent skill compatibility](../reference/agent-skill-compatibility.md) policy.
46	Local skills should target portable coding-agent limits: hyphen-case names
47	under 64 chars, descriptions under 1024 chars, and 120-500 chars preferred.
48	
49	## Required structure
50	
51	See [Conventions](../conventions.md) for the full layout rules. In short:
52	
53	- `SKILL.md` — required, lean (under ~500 lines).
54	- `assets/` — templates the skill copies into target projects.
55	- `scripts/` — executable helpers (Bash 3.2 compatible).
56	- `references/` — long-form material loaded on demand.
57	
58	## Author the SKILL.md following agentskills.io best practices
59	
60	The two highest-leverage rules from the
61	[agentskills.io best practices](https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/best-practices):
62	
63	1. **Procedures over declarations.** Tell the agent what to *do*, not what
64	   to *be*. A SKILL.md that says "follow these three steps" is much more
65	   reliable than one that says "be a careful and methodical helper".
66	2. **Defaults over menus.** Pick one workflow as the default; offer
67	   alternatives via flags or in `references/`. Letting the agent choose
68	   between three equivalent options at every step is a debugging nightmare.
69	
70	A third rule we apply in this repo:
71	
72	- **Bundle the workflow as a script if you can.** If the skill keeps asking
73	  the agent to perform the same multi-step procedure, write it as a shell
74	  script in `scripts/` and make the SKILL.md call the script. The
75	  [`project-knowledge-harness`](../skills/project-knowledge-harness.md)
76	  skill is the reference for this pattern.
77	
78	## Add a docs page
79	
80	Every local skill should also have a page under `docs/skills/<skill>.md`
81	that explains, for a human reader, what the skill is for, when it
82	triggers, and what it costs to use. The `SKILL.md` is the agent-facing
83	contract; the docs page is the human-facing pitch. Both are valuable.
84	
85	When you create the docs page, also link it from
86	[`docs/skills/index.md`](../skills/index.md) and from `mkdocs.yml`'s `nav:`
87	block at the repo root.
88	
89	## Test by installing into a scratch project
90	
91	```bash
92	mkdir /tmp/scratch && cd /tmp/scratch
93	git init
94	npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
95	```
96	
97	This pulls the new skill into `.agents/skills/` of a clean project so you
98	can verify the SKILL.md activates as you expect.
99
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Adding vendor skills
2	
3	Vendor skills are third-party skills cherry-picked from upstream repos
4	into [`skills/vendor/`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/vendor).
5	The [`vendor.yaml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/vendor.yaml)
6	manifest tracks each upstream source plus the last-synced date and commit
7	SHA, so re-syncing is reproducible.
8	
9	## Quick add
10	
11	```bash
12	./scripts/add-vendor.sh owner/repo/path/to/skill
13	
14	# Examples
15	./scripts/add-vendor.sh marimo-team/skills/skills/marimo-notebook
16	./scripts/add-vendor.sh vercel-labs/agent-skills/skills/next-js
17	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --name my-name --branch dev owner/repo/skills/some-skill
18	
19	# Group into a series subdir
20	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --series fullstack-nextjs vercel/vercel-plugin/skills/nextjs
21	
22	# Or via Makefile
23	make add-vendor SOURCE=owner/repo/path/to/skill
24	
25	# GitHub URLs also work
26	./scripts/add-vendor.sh https://github.com/marimo-team/skills/tree/main/skills/marimo-notebook
27	```
28	
29	This verifies the upstream path exists, adds an entry to `vendor.yaml`, and
30	syncs the skill immediately. Pass `--no-sync` to only add the entry without
31	downloading.
32	
33	**Dependencies:** `gh` (GitHub CLI, authenticated) and `yq` (YAML processor).
34	
35	## Series grouping
36	
37	When you're vendoring a coherent set of skills around a single tech stack
38	(e.g. Next.js + Supabase + shadcn), pass `--series <name>` so the skills
39	land in `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/` instead of being flat. The
40	`series` field is recorded in `vendor.yaml` and honored by `sync-vendor.sh`.
41	
42	```yaml
43	# vendor.yaml
44	- name: nextjs
45	  series: fullstack-nextjs              # ← optional, omit for flat layout
46	  upstream:
47	    owner: vercel
48	    repo: vercel-plugin
49	    path: skills/nextjs
50	    branch: main
51	  last_sync: { date: "...", commit: "..." }
52	```
53	
54	This results in `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/nextjs/SKILL.md`. The
55	`npx skills@latest add` discovery does a 5-level fallback recursive
56	search, so series subdirs are still discovered.
57	
58	Existing flat entries (no `series` field) keep working unchanged. Active
59	series in this repo:
60	
61	- **`fullstack-nextjs`** — see [Skills overview > Fullstack Next.js series](../skills/index.md#fullstack-nextjs-series)
62	
63	## Manual config
64	
65	If you'd rather edit `vendor.yaml` by hand:
66	
67	```yaml
68	- name: my-skill
69	  upstream:
70	    owner: org-name
71	    repo: skills-repo
72	    path: skills/my-skill
73	    branch: main
74	  last_sync:
75	    date: ""
76	    commit: ""
77	```
78	
79	Then run `make sync` to download and stamp `last_sync`.
80	
81	## Check for upstream updates
82	
83	```bash
84	make sync-check
85	```
86	
87	This dry-runs the sync against the recorded `last_sync.commit` for each
88	entry and prints which skills have new commits upstream. Run `make sync`
89	to apply.
90	
91	## Why not just install upstream directly?
92	
93	`npx skills add owner/repo/path/to/skill` works one skill at a time and
94	leaves no manifest. Vendoring into this repo gives you:
95	
96	- A single install command for the whole curated set
97	  (`npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`).
98	- A pinned commit per skill so a reckless upstream change doesn't surprise you.
99	- A diff in your repo when you re-sync, which is your chance to read what
100	  changed before accepting it.
101	
102	## Don't edit vendored skills in place
103	
104	Modifications under `skills/vendor/` get overwritten by `make sync`. If you
105	need to customize a vendored skill, fork it into `skills/local/` and drop
106	the upstream entry from `vendor.yaml`. See [Conventions](../conventions.md).
107
```
</details></tool-use>

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# new-skill.sh — Scaffold a new agent skill in the npx-skills-compatible layout.
3	#
4	# Three placement scopes (auto-detected by default, override with --local /
5	# --project / --global):
6	#
7	#   LOCAL    Publishing-repo workflow (this very repo). Canonical content lives
8	#            under <repo>/skills/local/<name>/ (or skills/vendor/<name>/ with
9	#            --vendor), and discovery symlinks are added at
10	#            <repo>/.agents/skills/<name> and <repo>/.claude/skills/<name>
11	#            -> ../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>.
12	#
13	#   PROJECT  Generic per-project install. Canonical content at
14	#            <repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/ (universal agents like Cursor /
15	#            Codex / OpenCode / Warp pick this up directly), plus a relative
16	#            symlink at <repo>/.claude/skills/<name> -> ../../.agents/skills/<name>
17	#            (and other already-present non-universal agent dirs).
18	#
19	#   GLOBAL   System-wide install. Canonical content at ~/.agents/skills/<name>/
20	#            plus a relative symlink at ~/.claude/skills/<name> ->
21	#            ../../.agents/skills/<name> (and any other detected agent dir).
22	#
23	# Auto-detection precedence (when no scope flag given):
24	#   1. publishing repo (vendor.yaml, skills/local/, or
25	#      skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json found walking up) -> LOCAL
26	#   2. inside a git repo (.git found walking up)                 -> PROJECT
27	#   3. otherwise                                                 -> GLOBAL
28	#
29	# Bash 3.2 compatible (works on stock macOS — no mapfile, no ${var,,},
30	# no [[ -v var ]]).
31	
32	set -euo pipefail
33	
34	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
35	SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
36	ASSETS_DIR="$SKILL_DIR/assets"
37	
38	usage() {
39	  cat <<'EOF'
40	Usage: new-skill.sh [OPTIONS] <skill-name>
41	
42	Scaffold a new agent skill with the standard layout (SKILL.md, references/,
43	scripts/, assets/) seeded from skill-author's templates, then place it where
44	the active scope says it belongs and add discovery symlinks for non-universal
45	agents.
46	
47	Scope (mutually exclusive — auto-detected if omitted):
48	  --local            Force LOCAL mode (this publishing repo's skills/local/).
49	                     Requires a vendor.yaml / skills/local/ / skills/.claude-plugin
50	                     anchor walking up from --root or CWD.
51	  --project          Force PROJECT mode (<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/).
52	                     Requires a git repo root (.git) walking up.
53	  --global           Force GLOBAL mode (~/.agents/skills/<name>/).
54	
55	Other options:
56	  --vendor           In LOCAL mode, place under skills/vendor/<name>/ instead of
57	                     skills/local/. (Rare — vendored skills normally come via
58	                     vendor.yaml + scripts/sync-vendor.sh.)
59	  --root DIR         Override repo / project root discovery.
60	  --no-symlinks      Skip the agent-dir discovery symlinks (just write the
61	                     canonical dir). Useful for CI / packaging tests.
62	  --dry-run          Print what would be created without writing.
63	  --force            Overwrite if the target canonical directory already exists.
64	                     Existing symlinks are always replaced.
65	  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.
66	
67	Examples:
68	  bash new-skill.sh my-skill                # auto-detect scope
69	  bash new-skill.sh --project my-skill      # force project (.agents/skills)
70	  bash new-skill.sh --global my-skill       # force user-wide (~/.agents/skills)
71	  bash new-skill.sh --local my-skill        # force skills/local/ (publish repo)
72	  bash new-skill.sh --dry-run my-skill      # see what would happen
73	  bash new-skill.sh --root /path/to/repo my-skill
74	
75	Output:
76	  Single JSON object on stdout (parseable by an agent), prose on stderr.
77	  Keys: skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[].
78	
79	Exit codes:
80	  0  success
81	  1  invalid arguments
82	  2  target canonical directory already exists (use --force to overwrite)
83	  3  scope precondition failed (e.g. --local outside a publishing repo,
84	     --project outside a git repo, template missing)
85	  4  symlink creation produced a broken link (post-write verification failed)
86	EOF
87	}
88	
89	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
90	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
91	
92	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
93	# Arg parsing
94	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
95	NAME=""
96	ROOT_OVERRIDE=""
97	DRY_RUN=0
98	FORCE=0
99	VENDOR=0
100	NO_SYMLINKS=0
101	MODE=""  # "", "local", "project", "global"
102	
103	set_mode() {
104	  if [ -n "$MODE" ] && [ "$MODE" != "$1" ]; then
105	    die "conflicting scope flags: already set to --$MODE, got --$1" 1
106	  fi
107	  MODE="$1"
108	}
109	
110	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
111	  case "$1" in
112	    --local)        set_mode local;   shift ;;
113	    --project)      set_mode project; shift ;;
114	    --global)       set_mode global;  shift ;;
115	    --vendor)       VENDOR=1; shift ;;
116	    --root)         ROOT_OVERRIDE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
117	    --no-symlinks)  NO_SYMLINKS=1; shift ;;
118	    --dry-run)      DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
119	    --force)        FORCE=1; shift ;;
120	    --help|-h)      usage; exit 0 ;;
121	    -*)             die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
122	    *)
123	      if [ -n "$NAME" ]; then
124	        die "only one skill name allowed (got '$NAME' and '$1')" 1
125	      fi
126	      NAME="$1"; shift
127	      ;;
128	  esac
129	done
130	
131	[ -n "$NAME" ] || die "missing <skill-name> (try --help)" 1
132	
133	# Validate name (kebab-case, no spaces, no leading dots).
134	case "$NAME" in
135	  -*|.*)            die "invalid skill name: '$NAME' (cannot start with '-' or '.')" 1 ;;
136	  *[!a-zA-Z0-9_-]*) die "invalid skill name: '$NAME' (use a-z, 0-9, _, -)" 1 ;;
137	esac
138	
139	if [ "$VENDOR" = "1" ] && [ -n "$MODE" ] && [ "$MODE" != "local" ]; then
140	  die "--vendor only makes sense in --local mode (publishing-repo workflow)" 1
141	fi
142	
143	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
144	# Scope discovery
145	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
146	
147	# Walk up from $1 looking for a directory matching the predicate (a callable
148	# that takes the candidate dir and returns 0 if it matches).
149	walk_up_for() {
150	  local start="$1" predicate="$2"
151	  local cur="$start"
152	  while [ "$cur" != "/" ] && [ -n "$cur" ]; do
153	    if "$predicate" "$cur"; then
154	      printf '%s\n' "$cur"
155	      return 0
156	    fi
157	    cur="$(dirname "$cur")"
158	  done
159	  return 1
160	}
161	
162	# Publishing repo marker: vendor.yaml at root, OR skills/local/, OR
163	# skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json.
164	is_publishing_anchor() {
165	  [ -f "$1/vendor.yaml" ] || \
166	  [ -d "$1/skills/local" ] || \
167	  [ -f "$1/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json" ]
168	}
169	
170	is_git_root() {
171	  [ -d "$1/.git" ] || [ -f "$1/.git" ]
172	}
173	
174	START_DIR="${ROOT_OVERRIDE:-$(pwd)}"
175	[ -d "$START_DIR" ] || die "start dir does not exist: $START_DIR" 1
176	
177	PUB_ROOT=""
178	PUB_ROOT="$(walk_up_for "$START_DIR" is_publishing_anchor 2>/dev/null || true)"
179	GIT_ROOT=""
180	GIT_ROOT="$(walk_up_for "$START_DIR" is_git_root 2>/dev/null || true)"
181	
182	if [ -z "$MODE" ]; then
183	  if [ -n "$PUB_ROOT" ]; then
184	    MODE="local"
185	  elif [ -n "$GIT_ROOT" ]; then
186	    MODE="project"
187	  else
188	    MODE="global"
189	  fi
190	fi
191	
192	# Validate scope preconditions and pick base + canonical dirs.
193	BASE_DIR=""
194	CANONICAL_PARENT=""
195	CANONICAL_DIR=""
196	SUBDIR_LABEL=""
197	
198	case "$MODE" in
199	  local)
200	    if [ -z "$PUB_ROOT" ]; then
201	      die "--local requires a publishing-repo anchor (vendor.yaml, skills/local/, or skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json) walking up from $START_DIR" 3
202	    fi
203	    BASE_DIR="$PUB_ROOT"
204	    if [ "$VENDOR" = "1" ]; then
205	      SUBDIR_LABEL="vendor"
206	      CANONICAL_PARENT="$BASE_DIR/skills/vendor"
207	    else
208	      SUBDIR_LABEL="local"
209	      CANONICAL_PARENT="$BASE_DIR/skills/local"
210	    fi
211	    CANONICAL_DIR="$CANONICAL_PARENT/$NAME"
212	    ;;
213	  project)
214	    if [ -z "$GIT_ROOT" ]; then
215	      die "--project requires a git repo (.git found walking up from $START_DIR). Use --global for ad-hoc skills outside any repo." 3
216	    fi
217	    BASE_DIR="$GIT_ROOT"
218	    SUBDIR_LABEL="agents"
219	    CANONICAL_PARENT="$BASE_DIR/.agents/skills"
220	    CANONICAL_DIR="$CANONICAL_PARENT/$NAME"
221	    ;;
222	  global)
223	    BASE_DIR="$HOME"
224	    SUBDIR_LABEL="agents"
225	    CANONICAL_PARENT="$BASE_DIR/.agents/skills"
226	    CANONICAL_DIR="$CANONICAL_PARENT/$NAME"
227	    ;;
228	  *) die "internal: unknown mode '$MODE'" 1 ;;
229	esac
230	
231	if [ -e "$CANONICAL_DIR" ] && [ "$FORCE" = "0" ]; then
232	  die "target already exists: $CANONICAL_DIR (use --force to overwrite)" 2
233	fi
234	
235	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
236	# Non-universal agent fan-out table
237	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
238	#
239	# Universal agents (cursor, codex, opencode, gemini-cli, github-copilot, warp,
240	# zed, amp, cline, antigravity, deepagents, dexto, firebender, kimi-code-cli,
241	# loaf, replit, universal) read .agents/skills directly and need NO symlink.
242	#
243	# This list mirrors the non-universal subset of vercel-labs/skills's
244	# src/agents.ts that we realistically need to fan out to. Format:
245	#
246	#   "<config-root>|<skills-subdir>"
247	#
248	# We always fan out to claude-code; for everything else, we only create the
249	# symlink if its config root directory ALREADY exists at the base dir (mirrors
250	# upstream's "don't create .windsurf/ unless it's actually used in this
251	# project" behavior). The leading config-root check is what makes this safe to
252	# call on a fresh machine.
253	
254	NONUNIVERSAL_AGENTS_IF_PRESENT="\
255	.windsurf|skills
256	.kilocode|skills
257	.kiro|skills
258	.junie|skills
259	.roo|skills
260	.aider-desk|skills
261	.augment|skills
262	.continue|skills
263	.cortex|skills
264	.crush|skills
265	.qoder|skills
266	.qwen|skills
267	.factory|skills
268	.codebuddy|skills
269	.openhands|skills
270	.trae|skills
271	.codemaker|skills
272	.codestudio|skills
273	.commandcode|skills
274	.codeartsdoer|skills
275	.zencoder|skills
276	.tabnine/agent|skills
277	.iflow|skills
278	.kode|skills
279	.pi/agent|skills
280	.lingma|skills
281	.mcpjam|skills
282	.adal|skills
283	.bob|skills
284	.forge|skills
285	.snowflake/cortex|skills
286	.rovodev|skills
287	.ona|skills
288	.mux|skills
289	.moxby|skills
290	.devin|skills
291	.pochi|skills
292	.neovate|skills
293	.terramind|skills
294	.tinycloud|skills
295	.reasonix|skills
296	.jazz|skills
297	.inferencesh|skills
298	.hermes|skills
299	.autohand|skills
300	.vibe|skills"
301	
302	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
303	# Helpers
304	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
305	
306	create_dir() {
307	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
308	    log "[dry-run] mkdir -p $1"
309	  else
310	    mkdir -p "$1"
311	  fi
312	}
313	
314	write_template() {
315	  local src="$1" dst="$2"
316	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
317	    log "[dry-run] cp $src -> $dst"
318	    return 0
319	  fi
320	  if [ ! -f "$src" ]; then
321	    die "template missing: $src" 3
322	  fi
323	  cp "$src" "$dst"
324	}
325	
326	substitute() {
327	  local file="$1"
328	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
329	    log "[dry-run] would substitute placeholders in $file"
330	    return 0
331	  fi
332	  # Bash 3.2 safe: sed -i with a backup, then drop the backup file (the BSD
333	  # vs GNU sed split is the reason we go through a .bak detour).
334	  sed -i.bak \
335	    -e "s/SKILL_NAME_PLACEHOLDER/$NAME/g" \
336	    -e "s/SKILL_TITLE_PLACEHOLDER/$(printf '%s' "$NAME" | tr '-' ' ')/g" \
337	    "$file"
338	  rm -f "${file}.bak"
339	}
340	
341	# Symlink at <linkdir>/<NAME> -> ../../<rel-target>, then verify the link is
342	# resolvable (test -e). All three placement scopes use the same fixed two-
343	# levels-up form because both <linkdir> and <canonical-parent> are exactly
344	# two levels under the base dir (.claude/skills/, .agents/skills/, etc.) —
345	# see pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md.
346	#
347	# Args: <link-skills-dir> <relative-target-suffix>
348	# Example: link_into "$BASE_DIR/.claude/skills" "skills/local"
349	#          -> creates .claude/skills/<NAME> -> ../../skills/local/<NAME>
350	link_into() {
351	  local link_skills_dir="$1" target_suffix="$2"
352	  local link_path="$link_skills_dir/$NAME"
353	  local relative_target="../../$target_suffix/$NAME"
354	
355	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
356	    log "[dry-run] mkdir -p $link_skills_dir && ln -snf $relative_target $link_path"
357	    SYMLINKS_CREATED="$SYMLINKS_CREATED
358	$link_path -> $relative_target"
359	    return 0
360	  fi
361	
362	  mkdir -p "$link_skills_dir"
363	
364	  # Replace any existing entry (symlink, broken symlink, dir, or file). We do
365	  # NOT recursively delete real content here on purpose — if the path is a
366	  # real directory, the user pointed --force at the wrong place.
367	  if [ -L "$link_path" ]; then
368	    rm -f "$link_path"
369	  elif [ -e "$link_path" ]; then
370	    if [ "$FORCE" = "1" ]; then
371	      rm -rf "$link_path"
372	    else
373	      die "would clobber non-symlink at $link_path (use --force to replace)" 2
374	    fi
375	  fi
376	
377	  ln -s "$relative_target" "$link_path"
378	
379	  if [ ! -e "$link_path/SKILL.md" ]; then
380	    die "created symlink is dangling: $link_path -> $relative_target (resolved from $link_skills_dir). This is the pitfall described in pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md." 4
381	  fi
382	
383	  SYMLINKS_CREATED="$SYMLINKS_CREATED
384	$link_path -> $relative_target"
385	}
386	
387	# Resolve the target suffix that all symlinks for the current mode share.
388	# - LOCAL:   skills/local  (or skills/vendor with --vendor)
389	# - PROJECT: .agents/skills
390	# - GLOBAL:  .agents/skills
391	target_suffix_for_mode() {
392	  case "$MODE" in
393	    local)   [ "$VENDOR" = "1" ] && printf 'skills/vendor\n' || printf 'skills/local\n' ;;
394	    project) printf '.agents/skills\n' ;;
395	    global)  printf '.agents/skills\n' ;;
396	  esac
397	}

399	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
400	# Scaffold the canonical directory
401	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
402	log "Mode:      $MODE"
403	log "Base:      $BASE_DIR"
404	log "Canonical: $CANONICAL_DIR"
405	
406	create_dir "$CANONICAL_DIR"
407	create_dir "$CANONICAL_DIR/references"
408	create_dir "$CANONICAL_DIR/scripts"
409	create_dir "$CANONICAL_DIR/assets"
410	
411	write_template "$ASSETS_DIR/SKILL.md.template" "$CANONICAL_DIR/SKILL.md"
412	substitute "$CANONICAL_DIR/SKILL.md"
413	
414	# .gitkeep so empty subdirs survive `git add`.
415	if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "0" ]; then
416	  for sub in references scripts assets; do
417	    if [ -z "$(ls -A "$CANONICAL_DIR/$sub" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
418	      : > "$CANONICAL_DIR/$sub/.gitkeep"
419	    fi
420	  done
421	fi
422	
423	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
424	# Fan-out symlinks
425	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
426	SYMLINKS_CREATED=""
427	TARGET_SUFFIX="$(target_suffix_for_mode)"
428	
429	if [ "$NO_SYMLINKS" = "1" ]; then
430	  log "Symlinks:  skipped (--no-symlinks)"
431	else
432	  if [ "$MODE" = "local" ]; then
433	    # In LOCAL mode also add the .agents/skills convenience link in addition to
434	    # .claude/skills, because this repo dogfoods .agents/skills as a discovery
435	    # farm even though it isn't a "consumer install".
436	    link_into "$BASE_DIR/.agents/skills" "$TARGET_SUFFIX"
437	  fi
438	
439	  # claude-code: always fanned out (most-used non-universal agent).
440	  link_into "$BASE_DIR/.claude/skills" "$TARGET_SUFFIX"
441	
442	  # Other non-universal agents: only if their config root already exists at
443	  # $BASE_DIR (mirrors upstream's "don't create .windsurf/ unless present"
444	  # rule). Use a heredoc rather than a pipe so the while-loop runs in the
445	  # parent shell — preserves SYMLINKS_CREATED mutations and lets `die` exit

447	  while IFS='|' read -r root_dir sub; do

450	    if [ -d "$BASE_DIR/$root_dir" ]; then
451	      link_into "$BASE_DIR/$root_dir/$sub" "$TARGET_SUFFIX"
452	    fi
453	  done <<EOF
454	$NONUNIVERSAL_AGENTS_IF_PRESENT
455	EOF
456	fi
457	
458	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
459	# Structured success output
460	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
461	if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
462	  log "Dry run complete. Re-run without --dry-run to actually create files."
463	  exit 0
464	fi
465	
466	# Build a JSON array of symlinks for the structured output. bash 3.2 safe.
467	json_symlinks() {
468	  printf '['
469	  local first=1 line
470	  # Read from a temp string; the while-loop body runs in the parent shell
471	  # because we use here-string, so we can mutate `first`.
472	  while IFS= read -r line; do

476	    printf '"%s"' "$(printf '%s' "$line" | sed 's/"/\\"/g')"
477	  done <<EOF
478	$SYMLINKS_CREATED
479	EOF
480	  printf ']'
481	}
482	
483	NEXT_STEPS="\"Edit $CANONICAL_DIR/SKILL.md to fill in description and workflow\",\"Run lint-skill.sh $CANONICAL_DIR to verify\""
484	
485	printf '{"skill":"%s","mode":"%s","canonical":"%s","symlinks":%s,"next_steps":[%s]}\n' \
486	  "$NAME" "$MODE" "$CANONICAL_DIR" "$(json_symlinks)" "$NEXT_STEPS"
487

```text
---
name: plugin-creator
description: Create and scaffold plugin directories for Codex with a required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, optional plugin folders/files, valid manifest defaults, and personal-marketplace entries by default. Use when Codex needs to create a new personal plugin, add optional plugin structure, generate or update marketplace entries for plugin ordering and availability metadata, or update an existing local plugin during development with the CLI-driven cachebuster and reinstall flow.
---

# Plugin Creator

## Quick Start

1. Run the scaffold script:

```bash
# Plugin names are normalized to lower-case hyphen-case and must be <= 64 chars.
# The generated folder and plugin.json name are always the same.
# Run from the skill root (the directory containing this `SKILL.md`).
# By default creates in `~/plugins/<plugin-name>`.
python3 scripts/create_basic_plugin.py <plugin-name>
```

2. Edit `<plugin-path>/.codex-plugin/plugin.json` when the request gives specific metadata.
   The scaffold starts with valid defaults and must not contain `[TODO: ...]` placeholders.

3. Generate or update the personal marketplace entry when the plugin should appear in Codex UI ordering:

```bash
# Personal marketplace entries default to `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`.
python3 scripts/create_basic_plugin.py my-plugin --with-marketplace
```

Only specify `--marketplace-name <name>` when the default `personal` marketplace name is already
taken or installed and you need to seed a different new marketplace file:

```bash
python3 scripts/create_basic_plugin.py my-plugin \
  --with-marketplace \
  --marketplace-name team-local
```

Only use a repo/team marketplace when the user specifically asks for that destination:

```bash
python3 scripts/create_basic_plugin.py my-plugin \
  --path <repo-root>/plugins \
  --marketplace-path <repo-root>/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json \
  --with-marketplace
```

When the user specifies a marketplace path, make sure that marketplace is actually installed before
telling the user to reinstall from it. The default personal marketplace file at
`~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` is discovered implicitly, but other marketplace paths are not.
On Windows, use the equivalent path under the user profile.

4. Generate/adjust optional companion folders as needed:

```bash
python3 scripts/create_basic_plugin.py my-plugin \
  --path <parent-plugin-directory> \
  --marketplace-path <marketplace-json-path> \
  --with-skills --with-hooks --with-scripts --with-assets --with-mcp --with-apps --with-marketplace
```

`<parent-plugin-directory>` is the directory where the plugin folder `<plugin-name>` will be
created (for example `~/plugins`).

5. Before handing back a generated plugin, run:

```bash
python3 scripts/validate_plugin.py <plugin-path>
```

For updates to an existing local plugin during development, keep the scaffold flow as-is and use the
reference instead of hand-editing marketplace files:

```bash
python3 scripts/read_marketplace_name.py
python3 scripts/update_plugin_cachebuster.py <plugin-path>
```

For a repo/team marketplace, pass `--marketplace-path <marketplace-json-path>` to the first command.
Prefer the helper default cachebuster unless the user explicitly asks for a specific override.
See `references/installing-and-updating.md` for the expected cachebuster and reinstall flow while iterating on an existing local plugin.

## What this skill creates

- Default marketplace-backed scaffolds use the personal marketplace file at
  `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, with plugins generally being stored in
  `~/plugins/<plugin-name>/`.
- Creates plugin root at `/<parent-plugin-directory>/<plugin-name>/`.
- Always creates `/<parent-plugin-directory>/<plugin-name>/.codex-plugin/plugin.json`.
- Fills the manifest with the validated schema shape that the ingestion path accepts.
- Creates or updates `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` when `--with-marketplace` is set.
  - If the marketplace file does not exist yet, seed a personal marketplace root before adding the first plugin entry.
- `<plugin-name>` is normalized using skill-creator naming rules:
  - `My Plugin` → `my-plugin`
  - `My--Plugin` → `my-plugin`
  - underscores, spaces, and punctuation are converted to `-`
  - result is lower-case hyphen-delimited with consecutive hyphens collapsed
- Supports optional creation of:
  - `skills/`
  - `hooks/`
  - `scripts/`
  - `assets/`
  - `.mcp.json`
  - `.app.json`

## Marketplace workflow

- Personal-marketplace creation defaults to `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`. Here,
  "personal marketplace" means the marketplace whose file is at that path.
- Repo/team marketplace creation is opt-in through both `--path` and `--marketplace-path`, only
  when the user specifically requests it.
- `--marketplace-name` is an exception path. Use it only when the default `personal` marketplace
  name is already taken and you need to seed a different new marketplace file.
- Do not use `--marketplace-name` to rename an existing marketplace file in place. If the file
  already exists, its top-level `name` must already match.
- If the user specifies a different marketplace path, treat that marketplace as needing explicit installation via `codex plugin marketplace add`.
- Plugin names must match `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)*`.
- Marketplace names must match `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`.
- For existing marketplaces, always validate names with `scripts/read_marketplace_name.py`; stop if
  validation fails. With no argument it reads the default personal marketplace; with an explicit
  path it works for repo/team marketplaces too. The scaffold validates new marketplaces itself.
- Before updating existing plugins, validate both identifiers before changing files or constructing
  install commands.
- In either location, the generated source path remains `./plugins/<plugin-name>`.
- Marketplace root metadata supports top-level `name` plus optional `interface.displayName`.
- Treat plugin order in `plugins[]` as render order in Codex. Append new entries unless a user explicitly asks to reorder the list.
- `displayName` belongs inside the marketplace `interface` object, not individual `plugins[]` entries.
- Each generated marketplace entry must include all of:
  - `policy.installation`
  - `policy.authentication`
  - `category`
- Default new entries to:
  - `policy.installation: "AVAILABLE"`
  - `policy.authentication: "ON_INSTALL"`
- Override defaults only when the user explicitly specifies another allowed value.
- Allowed `policy.installation` values:
  - `NOT_AVAILABLE`
  - `AVAILABLE`
  - `INSTALLED_BY_DEFAULT`
- Allowed `policy.authentication` values:
  - `ON_INSTALL`
  - `ON_USE`
- Treat `policy.products` as an override. Omit it unless the user explicitly requests product gating.
- The generated plugin entry shape is:

```json
{
  "name": "plugin-name",
  "source": {
    "source": "local",
    "path": "./plugins/plugin-name"
  },
  "policy": {
    "installation": "AVAILABLE",
    "authentication": "ON_INSTALL"
  },
  "category": "Productivity"
}
```

- Use `--force` only when intentionally replacing an existing marketplace entry for the same plugin name.
- If the target marketplace file does not exist yet, create it with top-level `"name"`, an `"interface"` object containing `"displayName"`, and a `plugins` array, then add the new entry.

- For a brand-new marketplace file, the root object should look like:

```json
{
  "name": "personal",
  "interface": {
    "displayName": "Personal"
  },
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "plugin-name",
      "source": {
        "source": "local",
        "path": "./plugins/plugin-name"
      },
      "policy": {
        "installation": "AVAILABLE",
        "authentication": "ON_INSTALL"
      },
      "category": "Productivity"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Required behavior

- Outer folder name and `plugin.json` `"name"` are always the same normalized plugin name.
- Do not remove required structure; keep `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` present.
- Do not leave `[TODO: ...]` placeholders in plugin manifests.
- Keep `apps` and `mcpServers` out of `plugin.json` unless their companion files are actually created.
- Omit unsupported plugin manifest fields that validation rejects, including `hooks`.
- If creating files inside an existing plugin path, use `--force` only when overwrite is intentional.
- Preserve any existing marketplace `interface.displayName`.
- When generating marketplace entries, always write `policy.installation`, `policy.authentication`, and `category` even if their values are defaults.
- Add `policy.products` only when the user explicitly asks for that override.
- Keep marketplace `source.path` relative to the selected marketplace root as `./plugins/<plugin-name>`.
- Only use `--marketplace-name` when creating a new marketplace file whose name should not be
  `personal` because that name is already taken or installed elsewhere.
- If Codex would need approval to write the marketplace file, ask for that approval before
  proceeding. If the user prefers to run the write themselves, provide the exact scaffold command
  and then continue from validation or subsequent plugin edits instead of leaving the workflow
  vague.
- For updates to an existing local plugin during development, do not hand-edit marketplace config
  or `marketplace.json`. Use the update flow documented in
  `references/installing-and-updating.md` and `scripts/update_plugin_cachebuster.py`.
- Do not tell the user to run `codex plugin marketplace add` for the default personal-marketplace
  flow. That command is for explicit non-default marketplace configuration, not for the standard
  `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` path.
- If the user provided a non-default `--marketplace-path`, make sure that marketplace is installed
  before giving reinstall instructions. Use `codex plugin marketplace add <path-to-marketplace-root>`
  when that explicit marketplace has not been configured yet.
- When the workflow created or updated a marketplace-backed plugin, end the final user-facing
  response with a short Codex app handoff. Say `To view this in the Codex app:` and write
  `View <normalized plugin name>` and `Share <normalized plugin name>` as Markdown links, not raw
  URLs or code spans.
- The View deeplink uses `codex://plugins/<normalized plugin name>?marketplacePath=<absolute marketplace.json path>`.
  The Share deeplink uses the same URL with `&mode=share`.
- Replace the placeholders with the real normalized plugin name and absolute `marketplace.json`
  path from the scaffolded plugin. URL-encode the path segment and query value when needed.
- Do not add `pluginName` or `hostId` query parameters to these deeplinks. Codex derives both after
  the user clicks the link.
- Do not emit the `View <normalized plugin name>` or `Share <normalized plugin name>` links when no marketplace entry was
  created or updated.

## Reference to exact spec sample

For the exact canonical sample JSON for both plugin manifests and marketplace entries, use:

- `references/plugin-json-spec.md`
- `references/installing-and-updating.md` for update/reinstall guidance while
  iterating on an existing local plugin, plus the new-thread pickup behavior after reinstall

## Validation

After editing `SKILL.md`, run:

```bash
python3 ../skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py .
```

Before handing back a generated plugin, run:

```bash
python3 scripts/validate_plugin.py <plugin-path>
```
```

`gh api -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github.raw+json' /repos/openai/codex/contents/codex-rs/skills/src/assets/samples/plugin-creator/references/plugin-json-spec.md`

```text
# Plugin JSON sample spec

```json
{
  "name": "plugin-name",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "description": "Brief plugin description",
  "author": {
    "name": "Author Name",
    "email": "author@example.com",
    "url": "https://github.com/author"
  },
  "homepage": "https://docs.example.com/plugin",
  "repository": "https://github.com/author/plugin",
  "license": "MIT",
  "keywords": ["keyword1", "keyword2"],
  "skills": "./skills/",
  "hooks": "./hooks.json",
  "mcpServers": "./.mcp.json",
  "apps": "./.app.json",
  "interface": {
    "displayName": "Plugin Display Name",
    "shortDescription": "Short description for subtitle",
    "longDescription": "Long description for details page",
    "developerName": "OpenAI",
    "category": "Productivity",
    "capabilities": ["Interactive", "Write"],
    "websiteURL": "https://openai.com/",
    "privacyPolicyURL": "https://openai.com/policies/row-privacy-policy/",
    "termsOfServiceURL": "https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/",
    "defaultPrompt": [
      "Summarize my inbox and draft replies for me.",
      "Find open bugs and turn them into Linear tickets.",
      "Review today's meetings and flag scheduling gaps."
    ],
    "brandColor": "#3B82F6",
    "composerIcon": "./assets/icon.png",
    "logo": "./assets/logo.png",
    "logoDark": "./assets/logo-dark.png",
    "screenshots": [
      "./assets/screenshot1.png",
      "./assets/screenshot2.png",
      "./assets/screenshot3.png"
    ]
  }
}
```

## Field guide

### Top-level fields

- `name` (`string`): Plugin identifier (kebab-case, no spaces). Required if `plugin.json` is provided and used as manifest name and component namespace.
- `version` (`string`): Plugin semantic version.
- `description` (`string`): Short purpose summary.
- `author` (`object`): Publisher identity.
  - `name` (`string`): Author or team name.
  - `email` (`string`): Contact email.
  - `url` (`string`): Author/team homepage or profile URL.
- `homepage` (`string`): Documentation URL for plugin usage.
- `repository` (`string`): Source code URL.
- `license` (`string`): License identifier (for example `MIT`, `Apache-2.0`).
- `keywords` (`array` of `string`): Search/discovery tags.
- `skills` (`string`): Relative path to skill directories/files.
- `hooks` (`string`): Hook config path.
- `mcpServers` (`string` or `object`): MCP config path, or an object whose keys are MCP server names and whose values are MCP server config objects.
- `apps` (`string`): App manifest path for plugin integrations.
- `interface` (`object`): Interface/UX metadata block for plugin presentation.

`mcpServers` may be declared as a companion file path:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": "./.mcp.json"
}
```

Or as an object directly in `plugin.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "counter": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://sample.example/counter/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

### `interface` fields

- `displayName` (`string`): User-facing title shown for the plugin.
- `shortDescription` (`string`): Brief subtitle used in compact views.
- `longDescription` (`string`): Longer description used on details screens.
- `developerName` (`string`): Human-readable publisher name.
- `category` (`string`): Plugin category bucket.
- `capabilities` (`array` of `string`): Capability list from implementation.
- `websiteURL` (`string`): Public website for the plugin.
- `privacyPolicyURL` (`string`): Privacy policy URL.
- `termsOfServiceURL` (`string`): Terms of service URL.
- `defaultPrompt` (`array` of `string`): Starter prompts shown in composer/UX context.
  - Include at most 3 strings. Entries after the first 3 are ignored and will not be included.
  - Each string is capped at 128 characters. Longer entries are truncated.
  - Prefer short starter prompts around 50 characters so they scan well in the UI.
- `brandColor` (`string`): Theme color for the plugin card.
- `composerIcon` (`string`): Path to icon asset.
- `logo` (`string`): Path to logo asset.
- `logoDark` (`string`): Optional path to the logo asset used in dark mode.
- `screenshots` (`array` of `string`): List of screenshot asset paths.
  - Screenshot entries must be PNG filenames and stored under `./assets/`.
  - Keep file paths relative to plugin root.

### Path conventions and defaults

- Path values should be relative and begin with `./`.
- `skills`, `hooks`, and string-valued `mcpServers` are supplemented on top of default component discovery; they do not replace defaults.
- Custom path values must follow the plugin root convention and naming/namespacing rules.
- This repo’s scaffold writes `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`; treat that as the manifest location this skill generates.

# Marketplace JSON sample spec

`marketplace.json` depends on where the plugin should live. New plugin creation defaults to the
personal marketplace unless the caller explicitly requests a repo-local destination:

- Personal plugin: `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`
- Repo/team plugin: `<repo-root>/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`

```json
{
  "name": "openai-curated",
  "interface": {
    "displayName": "ChatGPT Official"
  },
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "linear",
      "source": {
        "source": "local",
        "path": "./plugins/linear"
      },
      "policy": {
        "installation": "AVAILABLE",
        "authentication": "ON_INSTALL"
      },
      "category": "Productivity"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Marketplace field guide

### Top-level fields

- `name` (`string`): Marketplace identifier or catalog name.
- `interface` (`object`, optional): Marketplace presentation metadata.
- `plugins` (`array`): Ordered plugin entries. This order determines how Codex renders plugins.

### `interface` fields

- `displayName` (`string`, optional): User-facing marketplace title.

### Plugin entry fields

- `name` (`string`): Plugin identifier. Match the plugin folder name and `plugin.json` `name`.
- `source` (`object`): Plugin source descriptor.
  - `source` (`string`): Use `local` for this repo workflow.
  - `path` (`string`): Relative plugin path based on the marketplace root.
    - Personal plugin in `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`: `./plugins/<plugin-name>`
    - Repo/team plugin: `./plugins/<plugin-name>`
  - The same relative path convention is used for both personal and repo/team marketplaces.
    - Example: with `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, `./plugins/<plugin-name>` resolves to
      `~/plugins/<plugin-name>`.
- `policy` (`object`): Marketplace policy block. Always include it.
  - `installation` (`string`): Availability policy.
    - Allowed values: `NOT_AVAILABLE`, `AVAILABLE`, `INSTALLED_BY_DEFAULT`
    - Default for new entries: `AVAILABLE`
  - `authentication` (`string`): Authentication timing policy.
    - Allowed values: `ON_INSTALL`, `ON_USE`
    - Default for new entries: `ON_INSTALL`
  - `products` (`array` of `string`, optional): Product override for this plugin entry. Omit it unless product gating is explicitly requested.
- `category` (`string`): Display category bucket. Always include it.

### Marketplace generation rules

- `displayName` belongs under the top-level `interface` object, not individual plugin entries.
- When creating a new marketplace file from scratch, seed `interface.displayName` alongside top-level `name`.
- Always include `policy.installation`, `policy.authentication`, and `category` on every generated or updated plugin entry.
- Treat `policy.products` as an override and omit it unless explicitly requested.
- Append new entries unless the user explicitly requests reordering.
- Replace an existing entry for the same plugin only when overwrite is intentional.
- Default new plugin creation to the personal marketplace.
- Use a repo/team marketplace only when the user specifically requests that destination.
- Only override the marketplace `name` when the default `personal` name is already taken or
  installed and you need to seed a different new marketplace file.
- Choose marketplace location to match the selected destination:
  - Personal plugin: `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`
  - Repo/team plugin: `<repo-root>/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`

### Plugin validation notes

- The validator mirrors the workspace plugin ingestion schema so generated plugins follow the same
  manifest contract from the start.
- Plugin manifests must include real values for `name`, `version`, `description`,
  `author.name`, and the required `interface` fields.
- `version` must use strict semver.
- `websiteURL`, `privacyPolicyURL`, and `termsOfServiceURL` must be absolute `https://` URLs when
  present.
- `composerIcon`, `logo`, `logoDark`, and `screenshots` must point to real files inside the plugin archive when
  present.
- `apps` should appear in `plugin.json` only when `.app.json` actually exists.
- `mcpServers` may point to `.mcp.json` or contain the MCP server object directly in
  `plugin.json`.
- Validation rejects unsupported manifest fields such as `hooks`, so the scaffold keeps them out of
  generated manifests.
- Run `scripts/validate_plugin.py <plugin-path>` before handing back a generated plugin. It adds one
  intentional preflight check that rejects leftover `[TODO: ...]` placeholders.
```

```text
# Plugins

This repository contains a curated collection of Codex plugin examples.

Each plugin lives under `plugins/<name>/` with a required
`.codex-plugin/plugin.json` manifest and optional companion surfaces such as
`skills/`, `.app.json`, `.mcp.json`, plugin-level `agents/`, `commands/`,
`hooks.json`, `assets/`, and other supporting files.

The default marketplace lives at `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and points
at the standard `plugins/` directory. API key login users have a separate
marketplace at `.agents/plugins/api_marketplace.json`.

Highlighted richer examples in this repo include:

- `plugins/figma` for `use_figma`, Code to Canvas, Code Connect, and design system rules
- `plugins/notion` for planning, research, meetings, and knowledge capture
- `plugins/build-ios-apps` for SwiftUI implementation, refactors, performance, and debugging
- `plugins/build-macos-apps` for macOS SwiftUI/AppKit workflows, build/run/debug loops, and packaging guidance
- `plugins/build-web-apps` for deployment, UI, payments, and database workflows
- `plugins/expo` for Expo and React Native apps, SDK upgrades, EAS workflows, and Codex Run actions
- `plugins/netlify`, `plugins/remotion`, and `plugins/google-slides` for additional public skill- and MCP-backed plugin bundles
```

# Plugin Development Toolkit

A comprehensive toolkit for developing Claude Code plugins with expert guidance on hooks, MCP integration, plugin structure, and marketplace publishing.

## Overview

The plugin-dev toolkit provides seven specialized skills to help you build high-quality Claude Code plugins:

1. **Hook Development** - Advanced hooks API and event-driven automation
2. **MCP Integration** - Model Context Protocol server integration
3. **Plugin Structure** - Plugin organization and manifest configuration
4. **Plugin Settings** - Configuration patterns using .claude/plugin-name.local.md files
5. **Command Development** - Creating slash commands with frontmatter and arguments
6. **Agent Development** - Creating autonomous agents with AI-assisted generation
7. **Skill Development** - Creating skills with progressive disclosure and strong triggers

Each skill follows best practices with progressive disclosure: lean core documentation, detailed references, working examples, and utility scripts.

## Guided Workflow Command

### /plugin-dev:create-plugin

A comprehensive, end-to-end workflow command for creating plugins from scratch, similar to the feature-dev workflow.

**8-Phase Process:**
1. **Discovery** - Understand plugin purpose and requirements
2. **Component Planning** - Determine needed skills, commands, agents, hooks, MCP
3. **Detailed Design** - Specify each component and resolve ambiguities
4. **Structure Creation** - Set up directories and manifest
5. **Component Implementation** - Create each component using AI-assisted agents
6. **Validation** - Run plugin-validator and component-specific checks
7. **Testing** - Verify plugin works in Claude Code
8. **Documentation** - Finalize README and prepare for distribution

**Features:**
- Asks clarifying questions at each phase
- Loads relevant skills automatically
- Uses agent-creator for AI-assisted agent generation
- Runs validation utilities (validate-agent.sh, validate-hook-schema.sh, etc.)
- Follows plugin-dev's own proven patterns
- Guides through testing and verification

**Usage:**
```bash
/plugin-dev:create-plugin [optional description]

# Examples:
/plugin-dev:create-plugin
/plugin-dev:create-plugin A plugin for managing database migrations
```

Use this workflow for structured, high-quality plugin development from concept to completion.

## Skills

### 1. Hook Development

**Trigger phrases:** "create a hook", "add a PreToolUse hook", "validate tool use", "implement prompt-based hooks", "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}", "block dangerous commands"

**What it covers:**
- Prompt-based hooks (recommended) with LLM decision-making
- Command hooks for deterministic validation
- All hook events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact, Notification
- Hook output formats and JSON schemas
- Security best practices and input validation
- ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} for portable paths

**Resources:**
- Core SKILL.md (1,619 words)
- 3 example hook scripts (validate-write, validate-bash, load-context)
- 3 reference docs: patterns, migration, advanced techniques
- 3 utility scripts: validate-hook-schema.sh, test-hook.sh, hook-linter.sh

**Use when:** Creating event-driven automation, validating operations, or enforcing policies in your plugin.

### 2. MCP Integration

**Trigger phrases:** "add MCP server", "integrate MCP", "configure .mcp.json", "Model Context Protocol", "stdio/SSE/HTTP server", "connect external service"

**What it covers:**
- MCP server configuration (.mcp.json vs plugin.json)
- All server types: stdio (local), SSE (hosted/OAuth), HTTP (REST), WebSocket (real-time)
- Environment variable expansion (${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, user vars)
- MCP tool naming and usage in commands/agents
- Authentication patterns: OAuth, tokens, env vars
- Integration patterns and performance optimization

**Resources:**
- Core SKILL.md (1,666 words)
- 3 example configurations (stdio, SSE, HTTP)
- 3 reference docs: server-types (~3,200w), authentication (~2,800w), tool-usage (~2,600w)

**Use when:** Integrating external services, APIs, databases, or tools into your plugin.

### 3. Plugin Structure

**Trigger phrases:** "plugin structure", "plugin.json manifest", "auto-discovery", "component organization", "plugin directory layout"

**What it covers:**
- Standard plugin directory structure and auto-discovery
- plugin.json manifest format and all fields
- Component organization (commands, agents, skills, hooks)
- ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} usage throughout
- File naming conventions and best practices
- Minimal, standard, and advanced plugin patterns

**Resources:**
- Core SKILL.md (1,619 words)
- 3 example structures (minimal, standard, advanced)
- 2 reference docs: component-patterns, manifest-reference

**Use when:** Starting a new plugin, organizing components, or configuring the plugin manifest.

### 4. Plugin Settings

**Trigger phrases:** "plugin settings", "store plugin configuration", ".local.md files", "plugin state files", "read YAML frontmatter", "per-project plugin settings"

**What it covers:**
- .claude/plugin-name.local.md pattern for configuration
- YAML frontmatter + markdown body structure
- Parsing techniques for bash scripts (sed, awk, grep patterns)
- Temporarily active hooks (flag files and quick-exit)
- Real-world examples from multi-agent-swarm and ralph-wiggum plugins
- Atomic file updates and validation
- Gitignore and lifecycle management

**Resources:**
- Core SKILL.md (1,623 words)
- 3 examples (read-settings hook, create-settings command, templates)
- 2 reference docs: parsing-techniques, real-world-examples
- 2 utility scripts: validate-settings.sh, parse-frontmatter.sh

**Use when:** Making plugins configurable, storing per-project state, or implementing user preferences.

### 5. Command Development

**Trigger phrases:** "create a slash command", "add a command", "command frontmatter", "define command arguments", "organize commands"

**What it covers:**
- Slash command structure and markdown format
- YAML frontmatter fields (description, argument-hint, allowed-tools)
- Dynamic arguments and file references
- Bash execution for context
- Command organization and namespacing
- Best practices for command development

**Resources:**
- Core SKILL.md (1,535 words)
- Examples and reference documentation
- Command organization patterns

**Use when:** Creating slash commands, defining command arguments, or organizing plugin commands.

### 6. Agent Development

**Trigger phrases:** "create an agent", "add an agent", "write a subagent", "agent frontmatter", "when to use description", "agent examples", "autonomous agent"

**What it covers:**
- Agent file structure (YAML frontmatter + system prompt)
- All frontmatter fields (name, description, model, color, tools)
- Description format with <example> blocks for reliable triggering
- System prompt design patterns (analysis, generation, validation, orchestration)
- AI-assisted agent generation using Claude Code's proven prompt
- Validation rules and best practices
- Complete production-ready agent examples

**Resources:**
- Core SKILL.md (1,438 words)
- 2 examples: agent-creation-prompt (AI-assisted workflow), complete-agent-examples (4 full agents)
- 3 reference docs: agent-creation-system-prompt (from Claude Code), system-prompt-design (~4,000w), triggering-examples (~2,500w)
- 1 utility script: validate-agent.sh

**Use when:** Creating autonomous agents, defining agent behavior, or implementing AI-assisted agent generation.

### 7. Skill Development

**Trigger phrases:** "create a skill", "add a skill to plugin", "write a new skill", "improve skill description", "organize skill content"

**What it covers:**
- Skill structure (SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter)
- Progressive disclosure principle (metadata → SKILL.md → resources)
- Strong trigger descriptions with specific phrases
- Writing style (imperative/infinitive form, third person)
- Bundled resources organization (references/, examples/, scripts/)
- Skill creation workflow
- Based on skill-creator methodology adapted for Claude Code plugins

**Resources:**
- Core SKILL.md (1,232 words)
- References: skill-creator methodology, plugin-dev patterns
- Examples: Study plugin-dev's own skills as templates

**Use when:** Creating new skills for plugins or improving existing skill quality.


## Installation

Install from claude-code-marketplace:

```bash
/plugin install plugin-dev@claude-code-marketplace
```

Or for development, use directly:

```bash
cc --plugin-dir /path/to/plugin-dev
```

## Quick Start

### Creating Your First Plugin

1. **Plan your plugin structure:**
   - Ask: "What's the best directory structure for a plugin with commands and MCP integration?"
   - The plugin-structure skill will guide you

2. **Add MCP integration (if needed):**
   - Ask: "How do I add an MCP server for database access?"
   - The mcp-integration skill provides examples and patterns

3. **Implement hooks (if needed):**
   - Ask: "Create a PreToolUse hook that validates file writes"
   - The hook-development skill gives working examples and utilities

The plugin-dev toolkit supports your entire plugin development lifecycle:

           │

└──────────┬──────────┘
           │
┌──────────▼──────────┐

└──────────┬──────────┘

           │                 hook-linter.sh

## Features

### Progressive Disclosure

Each skill uses a three-level disclosure system:
1. **Metadata** (always loaded): Concise descriptions with strong triggers
2. **Core SKILL.md** (when triggered): Essential API reference (~1,500-2,000 words)
3. **References/Examples** (as needed): Detailed guides, patterns, and working code

This keeps Claude Code's context focused while providing deep knowledge when needed.

### Utility Scripts

The hook-development skill includes production-ready utilities:

```bash
# Validate hooks.json structure
./validate-hook-schema.sh hooks/hooks.json

# Test hooks before deployment
./test-hook.sh my-hook.sh test-input.json

# Lint hook scripts for best practices
./hook-linter.sh my-hook.sh
```

### Working Examples

Every skill provides working examples:
- **Hook Development**: 3 complete hook scripts (bash, write validation, context loading)
- **MCP Integration**: 3 server configurations (stdio, SSE, HTTP)
- **Plugin Structure**: 3 plugin layouts (minimal, standard, advanced)
- **Plugin Settings**: 3 examples (read-settings hook, create-settings command, templates)
- **Command Development**: 10 complete command examples (review, test, deploy, docs, etc.)

## Documentation Standards

All skills follow consistent standards:
- Third-person descriptions ("This skill should be used when...")
- Strong trigger phrases for reliable loading
- Imperative/infinitive form throughout
- Based on official Claude Code documentation
- Security-first approach with best practices

## Total Content

- **Core Skills**: ~11,065 words across 7 SKILL.md files
- **Reference Docs**: ~10,000+ words of detailed guides
- **Examples**: 12+ working examples (hook scripts, MCP configs, plugin layouts, settings files)
- **Utilities**: 6 production-ready validation/testing/parsing scripts

## Use Cases

### Building a Database Plugin

   → plugin-structure skill provides layout

   → mcp-integration skill shows configuration

   → hook-development skill provides pattern

```

### Creating a Validation Plugin

```
1. "Create hooks that validate all file writes for security"
   → hook-development skill with examples

2. "Test my hooks before deploying"
   → Use validate-hook-schema.sh and test-hook.sh

3. "Organize my hooks and configuration files"
   → plugin-structure skill shows best practices

```

### Integrating External Services

```
1. "Add Asana MCP server with OAuth"
   → mcp-integration skill covers SSE servers

2. "Use Asana tools in my commands"
   → mcp-integration tool-usage reference

3. "Structure my plugin with commands and MCP"
   → plugin-structure skill provides patterns
```

## Best Practices

All skills emphasize:

✅ **Security First**
- Input validation in hooks
- HTTPS/WSS for MCP servers
- Environment variables for credentials
- Principle of least privilege

✅ **Portability**
- Use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} everywhere
- Relative paths only
- Environment variable substitution

✅ **Testing**
- Validate configurations before deployment
- Test hooks with sample inputs
- Use debug mode (`claude --debug`)

✅ **Documentation**
- Clear README files
- Documented environment variables
- Usage examples

## Contributing

This plugin is part of the claude-code-marketplace. To contribute improvements:

1. Fork the marketplace repository
2. Make changes to plugin-dev/
3. Test locally with `cc --plugin-dir`
4. Create PR following marketplace-publishing guidelines

```text
1	# Agent skill compatibility
2	
3	This page records the cross-agent `SKILL.md` constraints this repo targets.
4	The goal is practical portability across coding agents, not the broadest set
5	of optional product-specific extensions.
6	
7	## Baseline we target
8	
9	Use the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) as
10	the portable baseline:
11	
12	| Field | Repo policy |
13	|---|---|
14	| `name` | Required, 1-64 chars, lowercase letters/digits with single hyphen separators, no leading/trailing hyphen, no `--`, should match the skill directory |
15	| `description` | Required, 1-1024 chars, describes both what the skill does and when to use it |
16	| `SKILL.md` body | Keep under ~500 lines; move long detail into `references/` |
17	| Optional frontmatter | Allowed only when a target agent needs it; keep local skills portable by default |
18	
19	Description budget tiers used by `skill-author`:
20	
21	| Tier | Length | Meaning |
22	|---|---:|---|
23	| Green | 120-500 chars | Preferred for local skills: enough trigger surface without context bloat |
24	| Yellow | 501-900 chars | Valid, but context-heavy; move details to the body or references |
25	| Orange | 901-1024 chars | Valid, but close to hard loader limits |
26	| Red | >1024 chars | Invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned validators |
27	
28	Also make the first 60 characters useful. The `npx skills` installer truncates
29	picker hints to 60 characters, and Codex may shorten descriptions when the
30	installed skill list is large.
31	
32	## Agent notes
33	
34	| Tool | Preference / constraint | Link |
35	|---|---|---|
36	| Agent Skills spec | Defines the portable directory layout, frontmatter fields, 64-char `name`, 1024-char `description`, optional `scripts/`, `references/`, and `assets/`. | [Specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) |
37	| Codex | Starts with each skill's name, description, and path, then loads full `SKILL.md` only when selected. The initial skills list has a context budget; descriptions should be concise and front-loaded. Codex can use optional `agents/openai.yaml` for UI metadata and invocation policy. | [Codex skills docs](https://developers.openai.com/codex/skills/create-skill) |
38	| Claude Code | Follows the open standard and adds fields such as `when_to_use`, `disable-model-invocation`, `user-invocable`, `allowed-tools`, `context`, and `hooks`. It truncates combined `description`/`when_to_use` listing text at 1,536 chars. | [Claude Code skills docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) |
39	| Cursor | Uses `SKILL.md` skills with the same practical 64-char `name` and 1024-char `description` budget in its managed `create-skill` guidance. It also supports `disable-model-invocation` for explicit-only skills. | [Cursor skills docs](https://cursor.com/docs/skills) |
40	| OpenCode | Recognizes `.opencode/skills`, `.claude/skills`, and `.agents/skills`; only specific frontmatter fields are recognized, unknown fields are ignored. It enforces 1-64 char names and 1-1024 char descriptions. | [OpenCode Agent Skills](https://opencode.ai/docs/skills/) |
41	| `npx skills` | Installer/distributor. Reads `name` and `description` from `SKILL.md`, shows only a 60-char description hint in the picker, and uses `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` for grouping. | [npx skills metadata model](npx-skills-metadata.md) |
42	
43	## How this repo applies it
44	
45	- Local skills should keep `description` in the green tier unless there is a
46	  concrete trigger-coverage reason to go longer.
47	- `skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh` enforces the portable hard
48	  limits: hyphen-case names, 64-char names, and 1024-char descriptions. It also
49	  reports yellow/orange tier notes without failing strict mode.
50	- `skills/local/skill-author/assets/SKILL.md.template` tells new authors to
51	  target 120-500 chars and never exceed 1024.
52	- Detailed trigger examples belong in `SKILL.md` body or `references/`, not in
53	  an oversized frontmatter description.
54	- Product-specific metadata is acceptable when needed, but should be deliberate:
55	  prefer portable frontmatter for local skills, leave vendored upstream metadata
56	  intact, and document any target-agent-only field in the skill body.
57	
58	## Incident that set the policy
59	
60	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap` previously had a 1106-character frontmatter
61	`description`. Codex 0.128.0 skipped it as invalid because the description
62	exceeded 1024 characters. We shortened the description to 489 characters and
63	updated `skill-author` so future local skills are caught before install-time
64	loader failures.
65
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# `npx skills add` ignores skills under `skills/local/` without `--full-depth`
2	
3	> **Update (skills@1.5.14):** the "`skills/local/*` are invisible" claim
4	> below is **stale**. The current CLI's priority walk reaches *two* levels
5	> under `skills/`, so depth-3 `skills/local/<name>/` and
6	> `skills/vendor/<name>/` are now discovered without `--full-depth`. What
7	> still breaks is **depth-4 series subdirs**
8	> (`skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`), and they break on `update` too — see
9	> [`skills-update-fails-for-series-nested-skills.md`](skills-update-fails-for-series-nested-skills.md).
10	> Kept below as history of the original (older-CLI) behavior.
11	
12	## Symptom
13	
14	```
15	$ npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills -g -s skill-author -y
16	...
17	■  No matching skills found for: skill-author
18	│
19	●  Available skills:
20	│    - find-skills
21	│    - skill-creator
22	```
23	
24	The skill clearly exists at `skills/local/skill-author/SKILL.md` in the
25	upstream repo, but `skills` CLI can't find it. Only skills sitting at
26	`skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (one level under `skills/`) are discovered.
27	
28	## Root cause
29	
30	The `npx skills` CLI (vercel-labs/skills) discovers skills by looking
31	**one level deep** under `skills/` for `SKILL.md`. If it finds at least
32	one match at that level, it stops. Recursive fallback **only** kicks in
33	when zero skills are discovered at the top level.
34	
35	This repo uses `skills/local/` and `skills/vendor/` to organize
36	custom-authored vs cherry-picked skills. Because `skills/vendor/` (and
37	indirectly `skills/local/`) doesn't put a `SKILL.md` immediately at
38	`skills/<name>/`, the CLI's default discovery goes:
39	
40	1. Check `skills/local/SKILL.md` and `skills/vendor/SKILL.md` → both
41	   missing.
42	2. Walk one level deeper: `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` and
43	   `skills/vendor/<name>/SKILL.md` → fallback recursive search finds
44	   `skills/vendor/skill-creator` and `skills/vendor/marimo-notebook`
45	   etc., **stops there**.
46	3. Never descends into `skills/local/<name>/`.
47	
48	So `skills/local/*` skills are invisible to `add` / `update` / `list`
49	unless the user explicitly opts into deeper discovery.
50	
51	## Workaround
52	
53	Pass `--full-depth` to force the CLI to keep walking even after it found
54	top-level skills:
55	
56	```bash
57	npx --yes skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills \
58	  -g -s skill-author -y --full-depth
59	```
60	
61	Verified to discover all four skills:
62	
63	```
64	✓ ~/.agents/skills/skill-author
65	  universal: Antigravity, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot ...
66	  symlinked: Claude Code, Continue, Droid
67	```
68	
69	## Prevention
70	
71	- Document `--full-depth` prominently in this repo's
72	  [`README.md`](../README.md) install snippet for any skill under
73	  `skills/local/`. The current snippet
74	  (`npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills`) installs only
75	  `skills/vendor/*` plus whatever's at `skills/<name>/`, silently
76	  skipping local skills.
77	- Alternatively: flatten `skills/` so all skills live at
78	  `skills/<name>/` directly. Trade-off: loses the visual local/vendor
79	  separation. The current nested layout is intentional (per
80	  [`docs/conventions.md`](../docs/conventions.md)) so flattening is
81	  not the preferred fix.
82	- For repo dogfooding (this same repo using its own skills via
83	  `.claude/skills/<name>` symlinks), CLI discovery doesn't matter —
84	  symlinks bypass the CLI entirely. Only matters when an outside
85	  user runs `npx skills add daviddwlee84/agent-skills`.
86	
87	## Where this was hit
88	
89	After authoring `skill-author`, ran
90	`npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills -g -s skill-author -y`
91	to install it globally. CLI reported "no matching skills" and listed
92	only `find-skills` + `skill-creator` (both from `skills/vendor/` because
93	the latter is at `skills/vendor/skill-creator/` which the fallback
94	recursive walk does find on its first pass — but it doesn't continue
95	into `skills/local/` after finding vendor entries). Adding
96	`--full-depth` fixed it. Found in commit `a365f30`'s preceding session.
97
```

```text
1	# `npx skills update` reports "Failed to update" for series-nested (depth-4) skills and leaves `.claude/skills` symlinks missing
2	
3	## Symptom
4	
5	Running `npx skills update` in a downstream project that installed skills
6	from this repo:
7	
8	```
9	Updating for: Universal, Claude Code
10	Refreshing 8 skill(s)...
11	
12	✗ Failed to check for deleted skills from daviddwlee84/agent-skills
13	Updating agent-history-hygiene...
14	  ✓ Updated agent-history-hygiene
15	Updating frontend-design...
16	  ✗ Failed to update frontend-design
17	Updating nextjs...
18	  ✗ Failed to update nextjs
19	...
20	Updating shadcn...
21	  ✗ Failed to update shadcn
22	Updating supabase...
23	  ✗ Failed to update supabase
24	
25	✓ Updated 4 skill(s)
26	Failed to update 4 skill(s)
27	```
28	
29	Key signal: **only the skills under a `vendor/<series>/` subdir fail** —
30	here `frontend-design`, `nextjs`, `shadcn`, `supabase`, all of which live
31	at `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/<name>/SKILL.md`. Everything at
32	`skills/local/<name>/` and `skills/vendor/<name>/` (one shallower)
33	updates fine.
34	
35	Second symptom — **agent symlink drift**. The project's
36	`.agents/skills/` (canonical Universal copies) has all 8 skills, but
37	`.claude/skills/` only has symlinks for the 4 that updated
38	successfully:
39	
40	```
41	$ ls .agents/skills/    # 8 real dirs
42	agent-history-hygiene  frontend-design  nextjs  project-knowledge-harness
43	shadcn  skill-author  skill-creator  supabase
44	$ ls .claude/skills/    # only 4 symlinks — the 4 that succeeded
45	agent-history-hygiene -> ../../.agents/skills/agent-history-hygiene
46	project-knowledge-harness -> ../../.agents/skills/project-knowledge-harness
47	skill-author -> ../../.agents/skills/skill-author
48	skill-creator -> ../../.agents/skills/skill-creator
49	```
50	
51	## Root cause
52	
53	`skills update` does not fetch skills itself — for each locked skill it
54	**spawns** the equivalent of:
55	
56	```
57	skills add daviddwlee84/agent-skills --skill <name> -y      # NOTE: no --full-depth
58	```
59	
60	`add`'s `discoverSkills()` without `--full-depth` does a *priority walk*
61	only: `skills/` → child (`local`/`vendor`) → grandchild (`<name>`). That
62	is **two levels under `skills/`**, so it discovers:
63	
64	- `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` ✓ (depth 3)
65	- `skills/vendor/<name>/SKILL.md` ✓ (depth 3)
66	
67	but **not** `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/SKILL.md` (depth 4) — the
68	series skill is a *great-grandchild* and is never walked. The recursive
69	`findSkillDirs` fallback that *would* reach depth 4 only runs when the
70	priority walk found **zero** skills; this repo has ~22 shallow skills, so
71	the fallback never fires.
72	
73	Because `update` hard-codes the spawn without `--full-depth`, there is
74	**no way to opt in from the `update` command** — the series skills fail
75	every time. `filterSkills` gets an empty match → `No matching skills
76	found for: frontend-design` → `add` exits 1 → `update` prints
77	`✗ Failed to update`.
78	
79	Reproduced with `skills@1.5.14`:
80	
81	```
82	without --full-depth :  Found 22 skills → "No matching skills found for: frontend-design"
83	with    --full-depth :  Found 47 skills → "✓ Installed frontend-design"
84	```
85	
86	Two knock-on effects:
87	
88	1. **Symlink drift.** `add` writes the canonical copy to
89	   `.agents/skills/<name>` and then (re)creates a symlink in every
90	   detected agent dir (`.claude/skills/<name>`) on *each successful*
91	   install/update. A skill that fails to update never gets its
92	   `.claude/skills` symlink — hence `.agents` has 8 but `.claude` has 4.
93	   This is *not* a first-install-only mechanism: a successful
94	   `add`/`update` always reconciles the symlinks, as long as the agent
95	   dir (`.claude`) exists at that moment.
96	2. **False "deleted skill" hazard.** `update`'s deletion check also runs
97	   `discoverSkills()` without `--full-depth`, so the series skills look
98	   absent and could be offered up for removal. In the run above the whole
99	   deletion block threw (`✗ Failed to check for deleted skills`) and was
100	   skipped — which accidentally saved them.
101	
102	Note: an older `pitfalls/skills-cli-skips-nested-skills-without-full-depth.md`
103	claimed `skills/local/*` were invisible without `--full-depth`. That is
104	**stale** for `skills@1.5.14` — the priority walk now reaches depth-3
105	`local/` and `vendor/`. Only depth-4 **series** subdirs are still missed.
106	
107	## Workaround
108	
109	Re-install the series skills once with `--full-depth`. This refreshes the
110	content, updates `skills-lock.json`, **and** creates the missing
111	`.claude/skills` symlinks (multiple `--skill` allowed):
112	
113	```bash
114	cd <downstream-project>
115	npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills \
116	  --skill frontend-design --skill nextjs --skill shadcn --skill supabase \
117	  -y --full-depth
118	```
119	
120	Plain `npx skills update` keeps working for every non-series skill; only
121	the series ones need this manual `--full-depth` refresh each time.
122	
123	## Prevention
124	
125	- **Preferred structural fix:** flatten the series so each skill sits at
126	  `skills/vendor/<name>/` (depth 3), where `update`'s shallow discovery
127	  finds it. The marketplace grouping is driven by
128	  `skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, not by directory depth, so
129	  flattening keeps the grouped install UI intact. Cost: touches
130	  `vendor.yaml` (`series:` field), `scripts/sync-vendor.sh`, and the
131	  `marketplace.json` paths.
132	- If the nested `vendor/<series>/<name>/` layout is kept, document that
133	  those skills can only be updated via
134	  `npx skills add … --skill <name> --full-depth`, never plain
135	  `npx skills update`.
136	- To keep `.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills` consistent, make sure the
137	  agent dir (`.claude/`) exists **before** the install/update that should
138	  populate it, and that the install actually succeeds — the CLI
139	  reconciles symlinks on every success, so a green install == a present
140	  symlink.
141	
142	## Where this was hit
143	
144	Downstream project `EcojoyComponents` ran `npx skills update` after
145	manually creating `.claude/`. The 4 `fullstack-nextjs` series skills
146	failed to update and never got `.claude/skills` symlinks; the 4
147	shallow-path skills updated and symlinked fine. Diagnosed by reading
148	`skills@1.5.14`'s `dist/cli.mjs` (`updateProjectSkills` → spawns
149	`add --skill` without `--full-depth`; `discoverSkills` priority walk) and
150	reproducing the 22-vs-47 skill count with/without `--full-depth`.
151	See also [`skills-cli-skips-nested-skills-without-full-depth.md`](skills-cli-skips-nested-skills-without-full-depth.md).
152
```
</details></tool-use>
