1	---
2	name: skill-author
3	description: Author a new agent skill or refactor an existing one to follow agentskills.io best practices — gotchas sections, output templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity (fragility-based), and agentic script design (--help, --dry-run, structured stdout, stderr diagnostics, PEP 723 inline deps, pinned uvx/npx versions). Use whenever the user wants to create a new skill from scratch, scaffold a SKILL.md, write a reference file, design a script meant to be invoked by an agent, lint a draft skill for quality, or convert an ad-hoc workflow into a reusable skill. For evaluating skill output quality with test cases, benchmarking, or optimizing the description trigger rate, defer to the `skill-creator` skill instead — this skill focuses on authoring, not evaluation.
4	---
5	
6	# Skill Author
7	
8	Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
9	https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
10	every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
11	once a draft exists).
12	
13	## When to use this vs `skill-creator`
14	
15	| Task | Use |
16	|---|---|
17	| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
18	| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
19	| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
20	| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
21	| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
22	| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |
23	
24	If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.
25	
26	## Workflow
27	
28	### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)
29	
30	Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:
31	
32	1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
33	2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
34	3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
35	4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)
36	
37	Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
38	description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.
39	
40	### 2. Scaffold
41	
42	Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout. The script
43	auto-detects **scope** (where to put the skill) and fans out discovery
44	symlinks for non-universal agents so the skill is loadable immediately.
45	
46	```bash
47	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
48	```
49	
50	Three scopes (auto-detected; override with `--local` / `--project` / `--global`):
51	
52	| Scope | Canonical dir | Symlinks created |
53	|---|---|---|
54	| **LOCAL** (this publishing repo: vendor.yaml / skills/local/ found walking up) | `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with `--vendor`) | `.agents/skills/<name>` + `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>` |
55	| **PROJECT** (inside another git repo) | `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents — Cursor / Codex / OpenCode / Warp — pick this up directly) | `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any already-present non-universal agent dir at the repo root) |
56	| **GLOBAL** (no git repo found) | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `~/.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any detected non-universal agent dir under `$HOME`) |
57	
58	The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
59	purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.
60	
61	> **Important**: When the user's intent is ambiguous (they're inside a git repo
62	> but haven't said whether the skill should live with the project or be
63	> available everywhere), **ask** "system-wide (`--global`) or just this
64	> project (`--project`)?" before running the script. The script is
65	> non-interactive — once you've picked a scope, files land and symlinks fan
66	> out without further prompting.
67	
68	After running, the script emits a single JSON object on stdout with
69	`{skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[]}` so you can chain
70	follow-up actions deterministically.
71	
72	### 3. Author the SKILL.md
73	
74	Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
75	that matter most:
76	
77	- **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
78	  descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills. Keep
79	  this within the cross-agent budget: 120-500 chars is the preferred range,
80	  501-900 is valid but context-heavy, 901-1024 is valid but close to hard
81	  loader limits, and >1024 is invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned skills.
82	- **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
83	  assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
84	- **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
85	  reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
86	- **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
87	  give the agent freedom (and explain *why*) where multiple approaches are valid.
88	- **Defaults, not menus** — pick one tool/approach and mention alternatives as
89	  escape hatches.
90	
91	Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. If you blow past that, move detail into
92	`references/<topic>.md` and tell the agent **when** to load it ("Read X if Y
93	happens"), not just that it exists.
94	
95	### 4. Design any scripts
96	
97	Before writing a script, read `references/script-design.md`. Skills script
98	design is meaningfully different from "regular" CLI script design because the
99	caller is an LLM reading your stderr to decide what to do next. The non-obvious
100	requirements:
101	
102	- No interactive prompts, ever (agents run in non-interactive shells)
103	- `--help` is the primary interface documentation — keep it concise but complete
104	- Errors must say *what was expected* and *what to try*, not just *what failed*
105	- Structured stdout (JSON/CSV/TSV), prose diagnostics to stderr — separate them
106	- `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
107	- Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations
108	
109	For Python helpers, prefer **PEP 723 inline dependencies** + `uv run` over
110	`requirements.txt` — the script becomes self-contained and the agent doesn't
111	have to set up an environment first.
112	
113	### 5. Lint
114	
115	Run the linter before committing or handing off to `skill-creator`:
116	
117	```bash
118	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
119	```
120	
121	It checks three things:
122	
123	1. **Frontmatter & length** — `name` and `description` exist; name is
124	   hyphen-case and <=64 chars; description has a "use when" trigger phrase,
125	   respects the 1024-char hard limit, and SKILL.md is under 500 lines.
126	2. **Script hygiene** — every `scripts/*.sh` has a shebang, is executable, and
127	   responds to `--help` (presence of the flag handler, not necessarily a working
128	   script).
129	3. **Reference reachability** — every file in `references/` is mentioned at
130	   least once from `SKILL.md` (no dead reference docs).
131	
132	Fix every error. Warnings are advisory but usually worth addressing.
133	
134	### 6. (Optional) Hand off to skill-creator
135	
136	Once lint passes and the skill *looks* right, the next questions are
137	quantitative: does it trigger reliably? does it produce good output? That's
138	`skill-creator` territory. Tell the user: "skill-author got the structure
139	right. If you want to validate it works on real prompts, the `skill-creator`
140	skill runs test cases and benchmarks."
141	
142	## Available scripts
143	
144	- **`scripts/new-skill.sh <name>`** — Scaffold the canonical skill dir
145	  (SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, assets/) and add discovery symlinks for
146	  non-universal agents. Auto-detects scope (LOCAL / PROJECT / GLOBAL); see
147	  table in step 2.
148	  - Scope flags (mutually exclusive): `--local` (force this repo's
149	    `skills/local/`), `--project` (force `<repo>/.agents/skills/`),
150	    `--global` (force `~/.agents/skills/`).
151	  - Other flags: `--vendor` (LOCAL only — `skills/vendor/<name>/` instead of
152	    `skills/local/`; rare, vendored skills normally come via `vendor.yaml`);
153	    `--root DIR` (override walk-up); `--no-symlinks` (skip the fan-out);
154	    `--dry-run`; `--force` (overwrite existing canonical dir + replace
155	    symlinks).
156	- **`scripts/lint-skill.sh <skill-dir>`** — Run frontmatter, script hygiene,
157	  and reference reachability checks. Exit non-zero on any error.
158	  - Flags: `--strict` (treat warnings as errors); `--quiet` (only print failures).
159	- **`scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh [PATH...]`** — YAML-parse the frontmatter of
160	  every `SKILL.md` under PATH (default `.`) with a real parser, and check that
161	  the root is a mapping with string `name` + `description`. Catches the
162	  breakage class `lint-skill.sh`'s awk extractor cannot see — an unquoted
163	  `description:` containing `": "` makes `npx skills` (and Claude Code /
164	  Cursor) **silently skip the skill**. `lint-skill.sh` calls this for the
165	  single-skill case; run it directly to sweep a whole collection.
166	  - Flags: `--parser auto|yq|python3|node` (`node` = the js `yaml` package,
167	    exactly what `npx skills` uses); `--quiet`.
168	
169	## Bundled assets
170	
171	Templates that `new-skill.sh` copies and that you can reference manually:
172	
173	- `assets/SKILL.md.template` — Frontmatter + workflow skeleton with placeholders.
174	- `assets/reference.md.template` — Reference doc skeleton (TOC + sections).
175	- `assets/script-bash.template` — Bash 3.2 compatible script with `set -euo pipefail`,
176	  `--help` / `--dry-run` flag handler, structured-output friendly logging
177	  (data → stdout, prose → stderr).
178	- `assets/script-python.template` — Python script with PEP 723 inline-deps
179	  block, argparse with help/examples, dry-run support.

1	# This-repo conventions
2	
3	Conventions specific to the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repository. Skills
4	authored elsewhere may follow different rules; this file is the source of
5	truth for **this** repo.
6	
7	## Layout
8	
9	```
10	skills/
11	├── local/             # skills authored in this repo (committed in full)
12	│   └── <skill-name>/
13	│       ├── SKILL.md
14	│       ├── references/
15	│       ├── scripts/
16	│       └── assets/
17	└── vendor/            # skills cherry-picked from upstream repos
18	    └── <skill-name>/
19	        └── ...        # synced via scripts/sync-vendor.sh
20	```
21	
22	- **New skills authored here go in `skills/local/`.** Always.
23	- **Don't manually edit anything in `skills/vendor/`** — it gets overwritten by
24	  the next `make sync`. Upstream changes go through `vendor.yaml` + `make sync`.
25	- **`.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` at the repo root are active
26	  discovery-symlink farms**, not legacy. Each entry under them is a relative
27	  symlink (`../../skills/local/<name>` or `../../skills/vendor/<name>`) so
28	  that Cursor / Codex / Warp / OpenCode (`.agents/skills/`) and Claude Code
29	  (`.claude/skills/`) can dogfood the skills authored in this repo. The
30	  `new-skill.sh` scaffolder creates these symlinks automatically in **LOCAL
31	  mode**; never add new *canonical* skill content directly under them here.
32	
33	## `new-skill.sh` placement scopes
34	
35	`scripts/new-skill.sh` supports three placement scopes that mirror the
36	behavior of `npx skills add` (`vercel-labs/skills`). Auto-detection
37	precedence (when no flag given):
38	
39	1. **LOCAL** — publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml`, `skills/local/`, or
40	   `skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) found walking up. This is the
41	   default *inside this very repo*. Canonical content lives in
42	   `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with
43	   `--vendor`); the script adds the `.agents/skills/` + `.claude/skills/`
44	   discovery symlinks for you.
45	2. **PROJECT** — a git root found walking up. Canonical content goes to
46	   `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents like Cursor / Codex /
47	   OpenCode / Warp / Gemini-CLI / Copilot read this directly); a relative
48	   symlink `<repo>/.claude/skills/<name> -> ../../.agents/skills/<name>` is
49	   added for Claude Code, plus links for any other non-universal agent dir
50	   (e.g. `.windsurf/`, `.continue/`) that already exists at the repo root.
51	3. **GLOBAL** — neither anchor found, or `--global` forced. Same shape as
52	   PROJECT but rooted at `$HOME`: canonical at `~/.agents/skills/<name>/`,
53	   plus `~/.claude/skills/<name>` and any other already-present
54	   `~/.<agent>/skills/` link.
55	
56	The fan-out rule is "claude-code always, others only if their config root
57	already exists at the base dir" — this mirrors `npx skills add`'s
58	"don't create `.windsurf/` unless the project already uses Windsurf"
59	behavior. The script never creates a new top-level agent home dir.
60	
61	Symlinks are always *relative* with a fixed `../../` prefix because both
62	the link's parent (`.../skills/`) and the canonical dir
63	(`.../.agents/skills/` or `.../skills/local/`) are exactly two levels under
64	the base dir. See [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md)
65	for the historical bug this convention prevents.
66	
67	## Skill discovery
68	
69	The `skills` CLI looks for `SKILL.md` files like this:
70	
71	1. **First pass:** one level deep — `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
72	2. **Fallback:** recursive up to **5 levels** if first pass found nothing
73	   useful.
74	
75	That's why `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` and `skills/vendor/<name>/SKILL.md`
76	both work — they're 2 levels deep, well within the recursive fallback. **Don't
77	nest a skill more than 5 levels deep** or it becomes invisible.
78	
79	## Scripts naming and mirroring
80	
81	Some scripts are bundled into a skill **and** mirrored to `scripts/` at repo
82	root. The pattern:
83	
84	| Canonical location | Mirror |
85	|---|---|
86	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/add-todo.sh` | `scripts/add-todo.sh` |
87	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` | `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` |
88	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/promote-todo.sh` | `scripts/promote-todo.sh` |
89	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/todo-kanban.sh` | `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` |
90	
91	Reason: the canonical copy travels with the skill (downstream consumers get it
92	via `init.sh`). The root-level mirror is for *this* repo's own use so `make`
93	targets and CI don't have to know the skill's path.
94	
95	**Mirrors must stay byte-identical.** If you edit one, run the equivalent
96	`cp` to update the other and verify with `diff`. There is currently no
97	automated check for this — be careful.
98	
99	## Documentation
100	
101	- `README.md` — short repo entrypoint with install snippet.
102	- `docs/` — built into a MkDocs Material site at
103	  `https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/`.
104	- `docs/skills/<skill-name>.md` — user-facing docs for each local skill. Link
105	  back to the canonical SKILL.md on GitHub via absolute URL (see linking rules
106	  in `docs/reference/docs-stack-recipe.md`).
107	
108	When you add a new local skill, also add:
109	
110	1. A row to `docs/skills/index.md`.
111	2. A `docs/skills/<skill-name>.md` page (can be short; cross-link to SKILL.md).
112	3. A nav entry in `mkdocs.yml`.
113	4. A row to the README's "What's in here" table.
114	
115	## Project memory
116	
117	This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` skill on itself. That means:
118	
119	- `TODO.md` is structured (P1/P2/P3/P?/Done sections, validated by
120	  `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`).
121	- `backlog/inbox.md` is the loose-capture inbox.
122	- `backlog/<slug>.md` holds research notes for non-trivial items.
123	- `pitfalls/<slug>.md` holds debugging traps with symptom-first titles.
124	
125	When authoring a skill, if you discover a non-obvious trap, write it to
126	`pitfalls/`. Don't bury it in commit messages or chat history.
127	
128	## AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md
129	
130	`AGENTS.md` is a **symlink** to `CLAUDE.md`. Edit either one. Don't replace
131	the symlink with a real file or they'll drift.
132	
133	## Bash compatibility
134	
135	All bundled scripts must be **bash 3.2 compatible** (stock macOS). See
136	`script-design.md` § "Bash 3.2 compatibility" for the safe subset and
137	escape hatches.
138	
139	## When this repo's conventions conflict with agentskills.io
140	
141	The agentskills.io best practices are upstream / generic; this file is local /
142	specific. When they conflict, this file wins **for skills authored in this
143	repo**. Notable specifics:
144	
145	- We default to bundling helper scripts in `scripts/` rather than relying on
146	  ad-hoc `uvx` invocations, because we want the helpers to compose with the
147	  repo's `Makefile` and CI.
148	- We use Bash for orchestration scripts (TODO management, vendor sync) so they
149	  run without a Python environment. PEP 723 Python is fine for analytical or
150	  parsing-heavy helpers.
151	- Skill descriptions in this repo lean **even pushier** than the agentskills.io
152	  guidance because we're optimizing for the OpenCode/Claude Code default
153	  triggering behavior, which under-triggers more aggressively than Claude.ai.
154

1	# Authoring patterns
2	
3	Condensed from <https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/best-practices>. Read this
4	before writing or editing a SKILL.md body.
5	
6	## Table of contents
7	
8	1. [Spending context wisely](#spending-context-wisely)
9	2. [Cross-agent frontmatter compatibility](#cross-agent-frontmatter-compatibility)
10	3. [Calibrating control](#calibrating-control)
11	4. [Gotchas sections](#gotchas-sections)
12	5. [Output templates](#output-templates)
13	6. [Checklists for multi-step workflows](#checklists-for-multi-step-workflows)
14	7. [Validation loops](#validation-loops)
15	8. [Plan-validate-execute](#plan-validate-execute)
16	9. [Bundling reusable scripts](#bundling-reusable-scripts)
17	10. [Quick checklist before commit](#quick-checklist-before-commit)
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Spending context wisely
22	
23	Every token in `SKILL.md` competes with the conversation history, the system
24	prompt, and every other active skill. Spend tokens on what the agent **wouldn't
25	know without you**:
26	
27	- Project-specific conventions (table names, repo layout, internal jargon)
28	- Domain-specific procedures with non-obvious steps
29	- Edge cases the agent will misjudge by default
30	- Specific tools/APIs to prefer (with the *why*, briefly)
31	
32	Don't spend tokens on:
33	
34	- Explaining what well-known things are (PDF, HTTP, REST, JSON)
35	- Generic "best practices" the agent already applies (handle errors, write tests)
36	- Comprehensive option enumerations — give a default and one escape hatch
37	
38	**Test:** for each paragraph, ask "would the agent get this wrong without it?"
39	If no, cut it.
40	
41	### Progressive disclosure
42	
43	Three loading levels:
44	
45	| Level | Loaded | Budget |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| Frontmatter (`name`, `description`) | always | 120-500 chars preferred, 1024 max |
48	| `SKILL.md` body | when skill triggers | <500 lines, <5000 tokens |
49	| `references/*.md`, `assets/*`, `scripts/*` | on demand | unlimited |
50	
51	If `SKILL.md` is creeping past 500 lines, move sections to `references/<topic>.md`
52	and reference them with **load conditions** ("Read X if Y happens"), not just
53	"see X for details". Conditions let the agent load on demand; bare pointers tend
54	to either get ignored or get pre-loaded out of caution.
55	
56	---
57	
58	## Cross-agent frontmatter compatibility
59	
60	Use this as the portable baseline for coding agents that consume Agent Skills:
61	
62	- `name`: required, lowercase letters/digits/hyphens only, no leading/trailing
63	  hyphen, no `--`, <=64 characters.
64	- `description`: required, non-empty string, <=1024 characters. Include both
65	  what the skill does and concrete trigger contexts. Keep the first 60
66	  characters meaningful because `npx skills` truncates picker hints there.
67	- **Quoting**: a YAML plain (unquoted) scalar may not contain `": "`, and ` #`
68	  starts a comment. Long English descriptions hit both constantly
69	  (`"…debug a FastAPI app: choosing def vs async def"`). Wrap such values in
70	  single quotes — the whole skill is otherwise skipped at install time with
71	  "Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings", or installs with a
72	  silently truncated description. `scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh` gates this.
73	- Keep `name` and `description` as the only required frontmatter fields for
74	  portability. Agent-specific fields are allowed when needed, but isolate them
75	  intentionally: Cursor uses `disable-model-invocation`, Codex can read
76	  `agents/openai.yaml`, and some vendored skills carry upstream-only metadata.
77	
78	Description budget tiers:
79	
80	| Tier | Length | Meaning |
81	|---|---:|---|
82	| Green | 120-500 chars | Preferred for local skills: enough trigger surface without context bloat |
83	| Yellow | 501-900 chars | Valid, but context-heavy; move details to `SKILL.md` body |
84	| Orange | 901-1024 chars | Valid, but close to hard loader limits |
85	| Red | >1024 chars | Invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned validators |
86	
87	Agent notes:
88	
89	- **Codex** skips invalid `SKILL.md` files; OpenAI's validator enforces the
90	  64-char name and 1024-char description limits.
91	- **Cursor** managed `create-skill` guidance matches the same 64/1024 limits
92	  and supports `disable-model-invocation` for explicit-only skills.
93	- **Claude Code** uses descriptions for discovery and tolerates additional
94	  frontmatter in practice, but long descriptions still consume always-on
95	  context and are poor picker hints.
96	- **OpenCode** follows the Agent Skills convention and uses descriptions for
97	  invocation; stay within the portable baseline unless a target agent's docs
98	  say otherwise.
99	- **Claude.ai upload** may impose stricter UI limits. Treat that as a separate
100	  packaging target, not the default coding-agent baseline for this repo.
101	
102	---
103	
104	## Calibrating control
105	
106	Match instruction specificity to **task fragility**, not to "we should be thorough".
107	
108	### Be prescriptive when:
109	
110	- The operation is destructive or has side effects
111	- A specific sequence of steps must hold (migration, release, deploy)
112	- An external system requires exact format (API contract, parser input)
113	
114	```markdown
115	## Database migration
116	
117	Run exactly this sequence:
118	
119	    python scripts/migrate.py --verify --backup
120	
121	Do not modify the command or add flags. The `--verify` step seeds an
122	integrity check that later phases depend on.
123	```
124	
125	The trailing sentence is the trick — even when prescriptive, **explain why**.
126	Agents that understand the reason follow it more reliably than agents that just
127	see "DO NOT" in caps.
128	
129	### Give the agent freedom when:
130	
131	- Multiple valid approaches exist
132	- The output is judgment-driven (code review, refactor proposal)
133	- You'd be hand-coding policy if you wrote it all out
134	
135	```markdown
136	## Code review process
137	
138	1. Check database queries for SQL injection (use parameterized queries)
139	2. Verify auth checks on every endpoint
140	3. Look for race conditions in concurrent code paths
141	4. Confirm error messages don't leak internals
142	```
143	
144	Notice: *what to look for*, not *how to look for it*. The agent picks the
145	approach.
146	
147	### Defaults, not menus
148	
149	When several tools could work, pick one default and mention alternatives as
150	escape hatches.
151	
152	```markdown
153	Use pdfplumber for text extraction.
154	
155	For scanned PDFs requiring OCR, fall back to pdf2image with pytesseract.
156	```
157	
158	…not:
159	
160	```markdown
161	You can use pypdf, pdfplumber, PyMuPDF, or pdf2image depending on...
162	```
163	
164	### Procedures over declarations
165	
166	Teach the agent *how* to approach the class of problem, not *what* to produce
167	for one instance.
168	
169	```markdown
170	Bad — only useful for this exact query:
171	  Join `orders` to `customers` on `customer_id`, filter region='EMEA',
172	  sum `amount`.
173	
174	Good — works for any query:
175	  1. Read schema from `references/schema.yaml` to find relevant tables.
176	  2. Join via the `_id` foreign key convention.
177	  3. Apply user-requested filters as WHERE clauses.
178	  4. Aggregate numeric columns and format as a markdown table.
179	```
180	
181	Specifics still belong in the skill (output format templates, "never output
182	PII", tool-specific quirks) — but the *approach* should generalize.
183	
184	---
185	
186	## Gotchas sections
187	
188	Often the single highest-value section in a skill. **Concrete corrections to
189	mistakes the agent will make without being told.** Not generic advice.
190	
191	```markdown
192	## Gotchas
193	
194	- The `users` table uses soft deletes. Queries must include
195	  `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` or results will include deactivated accounts.
196	- The user ID is `user_id` in the database, `uid` in the auth service, and
197	  `accountId` in the billing API. All three refer to the same value.
198	- The `/health` endpoint returns 200 if the web server is up, even if the
199	  database is down. Use `/ready` to check full service health.
200	```
201	
202	Keep gotchas in `SKILL.md`, not in a separate reference. The whole point is
203	that the agent reads them **before** hitting the situation — by the time it
204	realizes it should load `references/gotchas.md`, the bug has happened.
205	
206	**Iteration tip:** every time you correct the agent during a real run, add the
207	correction here. Most skills' gotchas sections grow over weeks, not get written
208	all at once.
209	
210	---
211	
212	## Output templates
213	
214	Agents pattern-match against concrete structures more reliably than they
215	follow prose descriptions. When the output has a fixed shape, paste the shape:
216	
217	````markdown
218	## Report structure
219	
220	Use this template, adapting sections as needed:
```

10	## Render the repo backlog
11

14	```bash
15	git clone https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills
16	cd agent-skills

18	```
19	
20	`make kanban` runs [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](reference/scripts.md#todo-kanbansh),

25	
26	The docs site you're reading is a [MkDocs Material](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/)
27	site. To preview it locally:
28	
29	```bash
30	# From the repo root
31	uv sync --extra docs
32	uv run mkdocs serve
33	```
34	
35	Then open <http://127.0.0.1:8000/>.

37	To produce the static site (what GitHub Pages serves):
38	
39	```bash
40	uv run mkdocs build --strict
41	```
42	
43	`make docs-serve` and `make docs-build` are convenience wrappers around
44	those two commands.
45	
46	## Apply the project-knowledge-harness skill to your own project
47	
48	If you just want the TODO + backlog + pitfalls structure in another repo,
49	the bundled init script does the whole setup in one shot:

```text
1	# Bundled scripts
2	
3	Every script in this repo's [`scripts/`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/scripts)
4	directory is also bundled inside the skill that owns it (so the package
5	shipped via `npx skills` stays self-contained). The pair must stay
6	byte-identical — see [Conventions](../conventions.md).
7	
8	Scripts are written in **Bash 3.2** so they run on stock macOS without
9	homebrew bash.
10	
11	## Vendor system
12	
13	### `add-vendor.sh`
14	
15	```bash
16	./scripts/add-vendor.sh owner/repo/path/to/skill
17	./scripts/add-vendor.sh https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/branch/path/to/skill
18	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --name custom --branch dev owner/repo/skills/some-skill
19	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --no-sync owner/repo/path/to/skill
20	```
21	
22	Verifies the upstream path exists via `gh api`, deduplicates against
23	existing entries in [`vendor.yaml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/vendor.yaml),
24	appends the new entry, and triggers `sync-vendor.sh` (skip with
25	`--no-sync`).
26	
27	**Dependencies:** `gh` (authenticated) and `yq`.
28	
29	### `sync-vendor.sh`
30	
31	```bash
32	./scripts/sync-vendor.sh           # download all vendored skills
33	./scripts/sync-vendor.sh --check   # dry-run: report which entries have new upstream commits
34	```
35	
36	Iterates `vendor.yaml`, downloads each skill via the GitHub trees API,
37	and updates `last_sync.{date,commit}` on success. `--check` prints what
38	would change without writing.
39	
40	## Project memory
41	
42	These ship with [`project-knowledge-harness`](../skills/project-knowledge-harness.md);
43	the canonical copies live at
44	[`skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts).
45	
46	### `todo-kanban.sh`
47	
48	```bash
49	./scripts/todo-kanban.sh                    # default: TODO.md, Markdown board
50	./scripts/todo-kanban.sh path/to/TODO.md    # explicit file
51	./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only    # exit code only, no rendering
52	./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --json             # machine-readable lane summary
53	```
54	
55	Validates the [TODO format](todo-format.md) and renders a kanban-style
56	board to stdout. Anything that's not a top-level `- [ ]` / `- ✅` item is
57	ignored, so you can sprinkle prose under section headings.
58	
59	Exit codes: `0` valid; `1` validation failure (line number printed to
60	stderr); `2` usage error.
61	
62	### `add-todo.sh`
63	
64	```bash
65	./scripts/add-todo.sh \
66	  --priority P3 \
67	  --effort M \
68	  --title "Add docs versioning" \
69	  --description "Use mike for versioned docs"
70	
71	./scripts/add-todo.sh \
72	  --priority "P?" \
73	  --effort "?" \
74	  --title "Try Rspress for docs" \
75	  --description "Evaluate AI-native docs framework alternative"
76	
77	./scripts/add-todo.sh \
78	  --priority P2 --effort L \
79	  --title "Migrate kanban to Python" \
80	  --description "Bash 3.2 compat is getting expensive" \
81	  --backlog
82	```
83	
84	Inserts a canonically-formatted entry into the matching `## P*` lane. With
85	`--backlog`, also scaffolds `backlog/<slug>.md` from the skill's template
86	and appends ` → [research](backlog/<slug>.md)` to the new line.
87	
88	After writing, re-runs the validator. If validation fails, the original
89	`TODO.md` is restored.
90	
91	Flags:
92	
93	- `--priority {P1|P2|P3|P?}` — required.
94	- `--effort {S|M|L|XL|?}` — required. `?` is only valid with `P?`.
95	- `--title TEXT` — required. Must not contain `*`.
96	- `--description TEXT` — required. Free-form after the em-dash.
97	- `--backlog` — also create the backlog research doc.
98	- `--file PATH` — TODO file (default `TODO.md`).
99	- `--dry-run` — print the rewritten file to stdout instead of mutating.
100	
101	### `promote-todo.sh`
102	
103	```bash
104	./scripts/promote-todo.sh \
105	  --title "<substring of the item's title>" \
106	  --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"
107	```
108	
109	Atomically moves an active item from its lane into `## Done` with the
110	dated `Done` syntax, then re-validates. Refuses to run if the substring
111	matches zero or more than one active item — refine the substring.
112	
113	Flags:
114	
115	- `--title SUBSTRING` — required. Case-sensitive substring of the title.
116	- `--summary TEXT` — required.
117	- `--file PATH` — TODO file (default `TODO.md`).
118	- `--date YYYY-MM-DD` — override completion date (default: today, UTC).
119	- `--dry-run` — print to stdout, don't modify.
120	- `--validator PATH` — override validator path (default: sibling `todo-kanban.sh`).
121	
122	### `sweep-inbox.sh`
123	
124	```bash
125	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh                # interactive triage of backlog/inbox.md
126	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh --dry-run      # preview without modifying inbox or TODO
127	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh --batch        # non-interactive: skip lines that need a prompt
128	```
129	
130	Reads [`backlog/inbox.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/backlog)
131	line by line. For each non-empty, non-comment line it prompts for the
132	priority / effort / formal title / description (defaulting where
133	possible), calls `add-todo.sh`, and removes the line from the inbox once
134	the entry is committed.
135	
136	`--batch` is intended for agent workflows: lines whose `priority:` /
137	`effort:` / `title:` / `description:` are inferable get formalized
138	automatically; ambiguous ones are left in the inbox for the next
139	interactive sweep.
140	
141	Inbox-line conventions (all optional; loose lines are also accepted):
142	
143	```text
144	# Comments and blank lines are ignored.
145	- maybe add docs versioning with mike
146	- priority=P3 effort=M title="Add docs versioning" desc="Use mike for versioned docs"
147	- the find-skills bootstrap UX is rough
148	```
149	
150	The first form requires interactive prompting. The second form is fully
151	parseable and works in `--batch` mode.
152	
153	### `init.sh`
154	
155	Lives only inside the skill (not mirrored to top-level `scripts/`):
156	[`skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/init.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/init.sh).
157	
158	```bash
159	skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/init.sh \
160	  --target /path/to/project \
161	  --project-name "My Project" \
162	  --deployment chezmoi   # or npm | pip | docker | none
163	```
164	
165	One-shot setup of `TODO.md` + `backlog/` + `pitfalls/` + agent guidance
166	snippet + README snippet for any target repo. Idempotent. See
167	[`project-knowledge-harness`](../skills/project-knowledge-harness.md) for
168	the full flag list.

171	
172	These ship with [`skill-author`](../skills/skill-author.md); the canonical

174	[`skills/local/skill-author/scripts/`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local/skill-author/scripts).
175	Not mirrored to top-level `scripts/` because they're agent-author tooling,

177	
178	### `new-skill.sh`
179	
180	```bash
181	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
182	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --project my-skill
183	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --global my-skill
184	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --vendor cherry-picked
185	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --dry-run my-skill
186	```
187	
188	Scaffolds the canonical skill directory (`SKILL.md` + `references/` +
189	`scripts/` + `assets/` from templates) and adds *relative* discovery
190	symlinks for non-universal agents. Auto-detects placement scope by walking
191	up from CWD; explicit flags override.
192	
193	Placement scopes (see
194	[creating local skills](../workflows/creating-local-skills.md) for the
195	full table):
196	
197	- **LOCAL** — publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml` / `skills/local/` /
198	  `skills/.claude-plugin/`) found. Canonical at `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/`
199	  (or `skills/vendor/` with `--vendor`); symlinks for `.agents/skills/` and
200	  `.claude/skills/`.
201	- **PROJECT** — `.git` found. Canonical at `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/`;
202	  symlink for `.claude/skills/<name>` (+ any already-present non-universal
203	  agent dir at the repo root).
204	- **GLOBAL** — neither anchor, or `--global`. Canonical at
205	  `~/.agents/skills/<name>/`; symlinks for `~/.claude/skills/<name>` and
206	  any other already-present non-universal agent dir under `$HOME`.
207	
208	The symlink fan-out matches `npx skills add`'s discipline: "claude-code
209	always, others only if their config root dir already exists at the base
210	dir" — never creates `.windsurf/` or similar for agents the user doesn't
211	actually use. Each created symlink is post-write verified with
212	`test -e <link>/SKILL.md`; a dangling link aborts with exit 4.
213	
214	Flags:
215	
216	- `--local` / `--project` / `--global` — force scope (mutually exclusive).
217	- `--vendor` — LOCAL only; use `skills/vendor/<name>/`.
218	- `--root DIR` — override walk-up start dir.
219	- `--no-symlinks` — skip the agent-dir fan-out.
220	- `--dry-run` — print every action without writing.
221	- `--force` — overwrite the canonical dir and replace any existing symlinks.
222	
223	Output: single JSON object on stdout
224	(`{skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[]}`); prose on stderr.
225	
226	Exit codes: `0` ok; `1` invalid args; `2` canonical dir already exists
227	(use `--force`); `3` scope precondition failed (e.g. `--project` outside
228	a git repo); `4` post-write symlink verification failed (the
229	[symlink-target-relative footgun](../reference/pitfalls.md)).
230	
231	### `lint-skill.sh`
232	
233	```bash
234	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<name>
235	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh --strict skills/local/<name>
236	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh --json   skills/local/<name>
237	```
238	
239	Lints a skill directory for frontmatter + length, script hygiene
240	(shebang / +x / `--help` handler), and reference reachability. See
241	[`skill-author`](../skills/skill-author.md) for the full checklist.
242	
243	### `lint-frontmatter.sh`
244	
245	```bash
246	make lint-frontmatter                                  # sweep skills/
247	./scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md
248	./scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh --parser node skills     # exact npx-skills parity
249	```
250	
251	YAML-parses the frontmatter of every `SKILL.md` under the given paths and
252	checks that the root is a mapping with string `name` + `description`.
253	`lint-skill.sh` delegates to it for the single-skill case.
254	
255	This exists because harnesses **silently skip** a skill whose frontmatter
256	does not parse — `npx skills add` prints `⚠ Skipped … YAML parse error` and
257	still exits `0`. The usual cause is an unquoted `description:` containing
258	`": "`; a ` #` in an unquoted value is worse, since it parses but truncates
259	the description at the comment marker (warning, not error). See
260	[pitfalls](../reference/pitfalls.md).
261	
262	Parser is auto-detected: `yq` → PyYAML → the js `yaml` package (what
263	`npx skills` itself uses; force it with `--parser node`). With none
264	installed the script degrades to a pattern heuristic and says so.
265	
266	Exit codes: `0` clean; `1` at least one file failed; `2` bad args, missing
267	path, or forced parser unavailable.
268	
269	### `git-hooks/pre-push`
270	
271	```bash
272	make install-hooks     # symlink it into .git/hooks/pre-push
273	git push --no-verify   # bypass once
274	rm .git/hooks/pre-push # uninstall
275	```
276	
277	Runs `make validate` (frontmatter + `marketplace.json` + `TODO.md` format)
278	and aborts the push on failure, printing the tail of the output. Mirrors
279	[`.github/workflows/validate.yml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/.github/workflows/validate.yml),
280	which runs the same three gates on push and PR — the hook just moves the
281	signal earlier, since a broken `SKILL.md` is invisible at install time.
282
```
</details></tool-use>

 `./docs/conventions.md`

```text
1	# Conventions
2	
3	These are the rules every local skill in this repo follows. They exist so
4	the package shipped via `npx skills` stays predictable and so adding a new
5	skill is mechanical, not a design exercise.
6	
7	## Local skill layout
8	
9	Each `skills/local/<skill>/` directory should contain:
10	
11	- **`SKILL.md`** — required, with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`)
12	  and a body that follows the
13	  [agentskills.io best practices](https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/best-practices)
14	  (lean SKILL.md under ~500 lines, defaults over menus, procedures over
15	  declarations).
16	- **`assets/`** — templates the skill copies into a target project
17	  (e.g. `TODO.md.template`, `pitfall-doc.md.template`).
18	- **`scripts/`** — executable helpers the agent should invoke instead of
19	  re-implementing logic in chat. Bash 3.2 compatible (so they run on stock
20	  macOS without homebrew bash).
21	- **`references/`** — long-form material the agent loads on demand
22	  (decision tables, schema cheatsheets, anti-pattern lists). Push detail
23	  here rather than swelling `SKILL.md`.
24	
25	## Mirror scripts to top-level `scripts/`
26	
27	Where a skill ships scripts that this repo also wants to run directly
28	(currently only [`project-knowledge-harness`](skills/project-knowledge-harness.md)),
29	copy them into the top-level [`scripts/`](reference/scripts.md) directory
30	so `make` targets and CI can invoke them. Keep the canonical copy inside
31	the skill so the package shipped via `npx skills` stays self-contained.
32	
33	The pair must stay byte-identical. The repo doesn't (yet) enforce this in
34	CI; if you edit one, edit the other in the same commit.
35	
36	## Vendor skill layout
37	
38	`skills/vendor/<skill>/` mirrors the upstream layout exactly. Don't edit
39	vendored skills in place — modifications get overwritten by `make sync`.
40	If you need to customize a vendored skill, fork it into `skills/local/`
41	and update [`vendor.yaml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/vendor.yaml)
42	to drop the upstream entry.
43	
44	## Documentation
45	
46	Every local skill should also have a page under `docs/skills/<skill>.md`.
47	The skill's `SKILL.md` is for the agent (concise, machine-aimed); the
48	`docs/skills/<skill>.md` page is for humans deciding whether to use it.
49	Both surfaces are valuable — don't try to merge them.
50	
51	Long-form references that the agent loads on demand
52	(`skills/local/<skill>/references/*.md`) can be mirrored or summarized
53	under `docs/reference/` when the audience extends to humans browsing the
54	site, but the canonical copy still lives next to `SKILL.md`.
55	
56	## Personal scratch areas
57	
58	`Collections.md` and `notes/` at the repo root are personal scratch space
59	for the maintainer and are intentionally not part of the published docs
60	site or the agent-facing surface. Don't link into them from `SKILL.md` or
61	from any docs page.
62
```
</details></tool-use>

    22

    25	Use the focused workflow's completion criterion when one applies. Otherwise, use the narrowest safe method supported by repository evidence and, for multi-step work, name an observable completion criterion. 1	---
2	name: agent-history-hygiene
3	description: Commit SpecStory chat transcripts (`.specstory/history/*.md`), Claude Code plan files (`.claude/plans/*.md`, `plansDirectory`), and other coding-agent artifacts (`.cursor/plans/`, `.cursor/rules/`, `.opencode/plans/`, `.specify/`, `.codex/`) alongside the feature diff they produced — without leaking `.env` contents, API keys, or private-key PEM blocks into git history. Use when the user says "commit my chat", "save this specstory session", "stage the plan file", "scrub the transcript", "my .env leaked in chat", "bootstrap pre-commit for this project", or when you notice untracked `.specstory/history/*.md` or `.claude/plans/*.md` files while running `git status`. Also use after an accidental push of a secret to enforce rotate-first, rewrite-last remediation instead of reflexive `git push --force`.
4	---
5	
6	# agent-history-hygiene
7	
8	Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
9	code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
10	`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.
11	
12	Three surfaces, separated by purpose:
13	
14	| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
15	|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
16	| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
17	| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
18	| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
19	| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
20	| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |
21	
22	## Core invariants
23	
24	1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
25	   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
26	   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.
27	2. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act
28	   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting
29	   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.
30	3. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a
31	   leak.** At best it's useless; at worst it destroys teammate work and
32	   silently re-introduces the secret when someone merges their old
33	   history back.
34	
35	## When to use this skill
36	
37	Use it when the user (or you) surface any of:
38	
39	- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "include the plan
40	  file in this commit" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
41	- You see dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
42	  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or any other configured agent artifact during
43	  `git status` and you're about to commit a feature.
44	- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
45	  chat history".
46	- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "I'm starting a new project — how
47	  do I get the hook stack?" / "bootstrap secret scanning here".
48	- "I pushed a `.env`" / "a secret went to main" / "do I need to force
49	  push?" — the agent must steer to `references/remediation.md` and
50	  stop the user from force-pushing reflexively.
51	
52	## When NOT to use
53	
54	- The user explicitly wants agent transcripts **excluded** from the
55	  repo. Respect that; suggest a one-liner `.gitignore` addition and
56	  skip this skill entirely.
57	- The leak is already on a shared `main`/release branch. Do **not**
58	  offer to rewrite history — jump to `references/remediation.md` §5.
59	- The project genuinely has no agent session (no `.specstory/`, no
60	  `.claude/plans/`, etc.). Nothing to stage.
61	- Single-file, single-commit hygiene that the agent handles without any
62	  script (e.g., adding a missing trailing newline).
63	
64	## Integration with existing infrastructure
65	
66	This skill sits **on top of** any chezmoi-managed stack the user
67	already has. It does not duplicate:
68	
69	- **chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath`** (`~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit`)
70	  — that wrapper runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and then
71	  optionally `gitleaks git --staged`. The skill bootstraps the repo-level
72	  config the wrapper expects to find.
73	- **chezmoi's `.gitleaks.toml`** — the user's config already carries
74	  curated rules for common API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Supabase,
75	  Linear, WakaTime, Cursor, HuggingFace, Notion, Tailscale, Clash /
76	  V2Ray tokens). The skill's `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` ships the
77	  same rule IDs so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist tweaks stay portable.
78	- **the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` hook** — the redactor ships as a
79	  pinned pre-commit hook from this repo
80	  (`.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`), so every consuming repo gets fixes via
81	  `pre-commit autoupdate` instead of a vendored copy that drifts. Details
82	  in [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md).
83	
84	What this skill **adds**:
85	
86	- Agent-facing discipline (this `SKILL.md` + `references/remediation.md`).
87	- A single-command project bootstrap (`bootstrap-project.sh`) for repos
88	  without chezmoi or where the user wants the stack in one go.
89	- Session-discovery heuristics (`find-session.sh`) for the "find my
90	  current transcript among many" problem.
```

156	## Adding a new local skill
157	
158	Use the bundled scaffolder (recommended — seeds the agentskills.io best-practice
159	template **and** fans out discovery symlinks for non-universal agents):
160	
161	```bash
162	# Auto-detects scope: LOCAL (this repo) / PROJECT (another git repo) / GLOBAL (~/).
163	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
164	
165	# Override scope explicitly when intent isn't obvious:
166	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --project <skill-name>
167	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --global  <skill-name>
168	
169	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
170	```
171	
172	The scaffolder mirrors `npx skills add`'s placement contract — canonical
173	content goes under `.agents/skills/<name>/` (read directly by Cursor /
174	Codex / OpenCode / Warp / Gemini-CLI / Copilot), with relative symlinks
175	fanned out to `.claude/skills/` and any other already-present
176	non-universal agent dir. In this repo (LOCAL mode) the canonical lives
177	in `skills/local/<name>/` and the symlinks point back at it. See
178	[Creating local skills](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/workflows/creating-local-skills/)
179	for the full scope table.
180	
181	Or, just the SKILL.md skeleton via the upstream init (no symlinks, no
182	`references/` / `scripts/` / `assets/`):
183	
184	```bash
185	cd skills/local
186	npx skills@latest init [skill-name]
187	```
188
```

96	## Marketplace Catalog
97	
98	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
99	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
100	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
101	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
102	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
103	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
104	for the full mechanism.
105	
106	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
107	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
108	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
109	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
110	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>` or
111	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
112	
113	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
114	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
115	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
116	frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
117	repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
118	`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
119	`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
120	within-group caveat in
121	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).
122	
123	## SKILL.md Format
124	
125	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.
126	
127	## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)
128	
129	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
130	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
131	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
132	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
133	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
134	
135	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
136	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
137	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
138	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
139	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
140	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
141	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
142	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
143	
144	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
145	
146	```bash
147	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
148	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
149	
150	# …or remove them afterward
151	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
152	```
153
```
</details></tool-use>

238	## Versioning
239	
240	- If `metadata.version` is **omitted** and the marketplace is hosted in
241	  git, every commit is treated as a new version — users always see
242	  whatever's on `main`. This matches `anthropics/skills`.
243	- If `metadata.version` is **set**, users only see updates when the
244	  number changes (semver-style).
245	
246	We currently set `metadata.version: "1.0.0"` as a baseline. To switch to
247	"every commit is latest" semantics, drop the field.
248	
249	## `marketplace.json` vs `plugin.json`
250	
251	| File | Purpose | When to use |
252	|---|---|---|
253	| `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | Catalog of multiple plugins / categories | Multi-category collections (this repo, `anthropics/skills`) |
254	| `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` | Manifest for a **single** plugin | Single-plugin repos (one bundle of skills, no grouping) |
255	
256	The two files are not redundant. `anthropics/skills` ships only
257	`marketplace.json`; we do the same. A repo can technically ship both,
258	but for a multi-category catalog like this one, `plugin.json` is
259	unnecessary.
260	
261	## Cross-agent portability
262	
263	`npx skills` is a one-way installer: it reads the manifest, then copies
264	SKILL.md files into each target agent's native skills directory
265	(supported targets enumerated in
266	[`src/types.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/types.ts)).
267	Other agents (OpenCode, Codex, Cursor, Aider, …) do **not** read
268	`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` natively — they have their own
269	conventions (`.opencode/`, `AGENTS.md`, `.cursor/rules/`, etc.).
270	
271	So the trade-off is:
272	
273	- One `marketplace.json` is enough for cross-agent **install** via
274	  `npx skills add`.
275	- Native discovery in non-Claude agents requires whatever that agent
276	  expects, separate from this manifest.
277	
278	If we ever need a second native catalog format, the cleanest
279	intermediate is to start treating `marketplace.json` as a *generated*
280	artifact from a canonical YAML and add a generator script. We have not
281	done that yet — single-consumer hand-edit is fine.
282	
283	## Hiding / deprecating a skill without deleting it
```
</details></tool-use>

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Skill Packager - Creates a distributable .skill file of a skill folder
4	
5	Usage:
6	    python utils/package_skill.py <path/to/skill-folder> [output-directory]
7	
8	Example:
9	    python utils/package_skill.py skills/public/my-skill
10	    python utils/package_skill.py skills/public/my-skill ./dist
11	"""
12	
13	import fnmatch
14	import sys
15	import zipfile
16	from pathlib import Path
17	from scripts.quick_validate import validate_skill
18	
19	# Patterns to exclude when packaging skills.
20	EXCLUDE_DIRS = {"__pycache__", "node_modules"}
21	EXCLUDE_GLOBS = {"*.pyc"}
22	EXCLUDE_FILES = {".DS_Store"}
23	# Directories excluded only at the skill root (not when nested deeper).
24	ROOT_EXCLUDE_DIRS = {"evals"}
25	
26	
27	def should_exclude(rel_path: Path) -> bool:
28	    """Check if a path should be excluded from packaging."""
29	    parts = rel_path.parts
30	    if any(part in EXCLUDE_DIRS for part in parts):
31	        return True
32	    # rel_path is relative to skill_path.parent, so parts[0] is the skill
33	    # folder name and parts[1] (if present) is the first subdir.
34	    if len(parts) > 1 and parts[1] in ROOT_EXCLUDE_DIRS:
35	        return True
36	    name = rel_path.name
37	    if name in EXCLUDE_FILES:
38	        return True
39	    return any(fnmatch.fnmatch(name, pat) for pat in EXCLUDE_GLOBS)
40	
41	
42	def package_skill(skill_path, output_dir=None):
43	    """
44	    Package a skill folder into a .skill file.
45	
46	    Args:
47	        skill_path: Path to the skill folder
48	        output_dir: Optional output directory for the .skill file (defaults to current directory)
49	
50	    Returns:
51	        Path to the created .skill file, or None if error
52	    """
53	    skill_path = Path(skill_path).resolve()
54	
55	    # Validate skill folder exists
56	    if not skill_path.exists():
57	        print(f"❌ Error: Skill folder not found: {skill_path}")
58	        return None
59	
60	    if not skill_path.is_dir():
61	        print(f"❌ Error: Path is not a directory: {skill_path}")
62	        return None
63	
64	    # Validate SKILL.md exists
65	    skill_md = skill_path / "SKILL.md"
66	    if not skill_md.exists():
67	        print(f"❌ Error: SKILL.md not found in {skill_path}")
68	        return None
69	
70	    # Run validation before packaging
71	    print("🔍 Validating skill...")
72	    valid, message = validate_skill(skill_path)
73	    if not valid:
74	        print(f"❌ Validation failed: {message}")
75	        print("   Please fix the validation errors before packaging.")
76	        return None
77	    print(f"✅ {message}\n")
78	
79	    # Determine output location
80	    skill_name = skill_path.name
81	    if output_dir:
82	        output_path = Path(output_dir).resolve()
83	        output_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
84	    else:
85	        output_path = Path.cwd()
86	
87	    skill_filename = output_path / f"{skill_name}.skill"
88	
89	    # Create the .skill file (zip format)
90	    try:
91	        with zipfile.ZipFile(skill_filename, 'w', zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zipf:
92	            # Walk through the skill directory, excluding build artifacts
93	            for file_path in skill_path.rglob('*'):
94	                if not file_path.is_file():
95	                    continue
96	                arcname = file_path.relative_to(skill_path.parent)
97	                if should_exclude(arcname):
98	                    print(f"  Skipped: {arcname}")
99	                    continue
100	                zipf.write(file_path, arcname)
101	                print(f"  Added: {arcname}")
102	
103	        print(f"\n✅ Successfully packaged skill to: {skill_filename}")
104	        return skill_filename
105	
106	    except Exception as e:
107	        print(f"❌ Error creating .skill file: {e}")
108	        return None
109	
110	
111	def main():
112	    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
113	        print("Usage: python utils/package_skill.py <path/to/skill-folder> [output-directory]")
114	        print("\nExample:")
115	        print("  python utils/package_skill.py skills/public/my-skill")
116	        print("  python utils/package_skill.py skills/public/my-skill ./dist")
117	        sys.exit(1)
118	
119	    skill_path = sys.argv[1]
120	    output_dir = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
121	
122	    print(f"📦 Packaging skill: {skill_path}")
123	    if output_dir:
124	        print(f"   Output directory: {output_dir}")
125	    print()
126	
127	    result = package_skill(skill_path, output_dir)
128	
129	    if result:
130	        sys.exit(0)
131	    else:
132	        sys.exit(1)
133	
134	
135	if __name__ == "__main__":
136	    main()
137

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Quick validation script for skills - minimal version
4	"""
5	
6	import sys
7	import os
8	import re
9	import yaml
10	from pathlib import Path
11	
12	def validate_skill(skill_path):
13	    """Basic validation of a skill"""
14	    skill_path = Path(skill_path)
15	
16	    # Check SKILL.md exists
17	    skill_md = skill_path / 'SKILL.md'
18	    if not skill_md.exists():
19	        return False, "SKILL.md not found"
20	
21	    # Read and validate frontmatter
22	    content = skill_md.read_text()
23	    if not content.startswith('---'):
24	        return False, "No YAML frontmatter found"
25	
26	    # Extract frontmatter
27	    match = re.match(r'^---\n(.*?)\n---', content, re.DOTALL)
28	    if not match:
29	        return False, "Invalid frontmatter format"
30	
31	    frontmatter_text = match.group(1)
32	
33	    # Parse YAML frontmatter
34	    try:
35	        frontmatter = yaml.safe_load(frontmatter_text)
36	        if not isinstance(frontmatter, dict):
37	            return False, "Frontmatter must be a YAML dictionary"
38	    except yaml.YAMLError as e:
39	        return False, f"Invalid YAML in frontmatter: {e}"
40	
41	    # Define allowed properties
42	    ALLOWED_PROPERTIES = {'name', 'description', 'license', 'allowed-tools', 'metadata', 'compatibility'}
43	
44	    # Check for unexpected properties (excluding nested keys under metadata)
45	    unexpected_keys = set(frontmatter.keys()) - ALLOWED_PROPERTIES
46	    if unexpected_keys:
47	        return False, (
48	            f"Unexpected key(s) in SKILL.md frontmatter: {', '.join(sorted(unexpected_keys))}. "
49	            f"Allowed properties are: {', '.join(sorted(ALLOWED_PROPERTIES))}"
50	        )
51	
52	    # Check required fields
53	    if 'name' not in frontmatter:
54	        return False, "Missing 'name' in frontmatter"
55	    if 'description' not in frontmatter:
56	        return False, "Missing 'description' in frontmatter"
57	
58	    # Extract name for validation
59	    name = frontmatter.get('name', '')
60	    if not isinstance(name, str):
61	        return False, f"Name must be a string, got {type(name).__name__}"
62	    name = name.strip()
63	    if name:
64	        # Check naming convention (kebab-case: lowercase with hyphens)
65	        if not re.match(r'^[a-z0-9-]+$', name):
66	            return False, f"Name '{name}' should be kebab-case (lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens only)"
67	        if name.startswith('-') or name.endswith('-') or '--' in name:
68	            return False, f"Name '{name}' cannot start/end with hyphen or contain consecutive hyphens"
69	        # Check name length (max 64 characters per spec)
70	        if len(name) > 64:
71	            return False, f"Name is too long ({len(name)} characters). Maximum is 64 characters."
72	
73	    # Extract and validate description
74	    description = frontmatter.get('description', '')
75	    if not isinstance(description, str):
76	        return False, f"Description must be a string, got {type(description).__name__}"
77	    description = description.strip()
78	    if description:
79	        # Check for angle brackets
80	        if '<' in description or '>' in description:
81	            return False, "Description cannot contain angle brackets (< or >)"
82	        # Check description length (max 1024 characters per spec)
83	        if len(description) > 1024:
84	            return False, f"Description is too long ({len(description)} characters). Maximum is 1024 characters."
85	
86	    # Validate compatibility field if present (optional)
87	    compatibility = frontmatter.get('compatibility', '')
88	    if compatibility:
89	        if not isinstance(compatibility, str):
90	            return False, f"Compatibility must be a string, got {type(compatibility).__name__}"
91	        if len(compatibility) > 500:
92	            return False, f"Compatibility is too long ({len(compatibility)} characters). Maximum is 500 characters."
93	
94	    return True, "Skill is valid!"
95	
96	if __name__ == "__main__":
97	    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
98	        print("Usage: python quick_validate.py <skill_directory>")
99	        sys.exit(1)
100	    
101	    valid, message = validate_skill(sys.argv[1])
102	    print(message)
103	    sys.exit(0 if valid else 1)

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="Read"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./pitfalls/skill-description-colon-breaks-yaml-frontmatter.md`

```text
1	# `npx skills` skips a skill: "YAML parse error: Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings"
2	
3	## Symptom
4	
5	`npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills` clones fine, then
6	quietly drops skills from the picker:
7	
8	```
9	⚠ Skipped /var/folders/.../skills/local/fastapi-ai-patterns/SKILL.md — YAML parse error: Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings at line 2, column 14:
10	
11	description: Production patterns and gotchas for building FastAPI services, esp…
12	             ^
13	
14	◇  Found 56 skills
15	```
16	
17	The install still "succeeds" — the skipped skills simply never appear in the
18	selection UI, and no non-zero exit code is returned. Three skills were being
19	dropped this way (`fastapi-ai-patterns`, `fastapi-ai-scaffold`,
20	`verifiable-surfaces`) before anyone noticed.
21	
22	The caret points at column 14, i.e. the start of the *value* — misleading,
23	because the actual offending character is much further right.
24	
25	## Root cause
26	
27	An unquoted YAML value (a *plain scalar*) may not contain `": "`. YAML reads
28	the first colon-space as a key/value separator, i.e. a nested mapping inside a
29	value that is already a mapping value — which is illegal in flow ("compact")
30	context:
31	
32	```yaml
33	description: Use when you build, review, or debug a FastAPI app: choosing def vs async def
34	#                                                              ^ second mapping separator → parse error
35	```
36	
37	All three broken descriptions used the same natural-English pattern —
38	`"…, or setting up a model-serving API with the production basics pre-wired: router/service…"`,
39	`"The invariant: a surface that cannot be exercised…"`. Colon-space is very
40	easy to write in a long description and there is no visual cue that it breaks
41	the file.
42	
43	Why it went unnoticed for so long:
44	
45	- `skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh` read frontmatter with a
46	  permissive `awk` extractor, so the skill "passed" its own lint.
47	- `make marketplace` only validates that paths exist and contain a `SKILL.md`
48	  — not that the file parses.
49	- Claude Code loaded the skills in-repo anyway (via the `.claude/skills/`
50	  discovery symlinks), so local dogfooding never surfaced the problem. Only a
51	  real `npx skills add` run does.
52	
53	## Workaround
54	
55	Wrap the value in single quotes. Nothing inside a single-quoted YAML scalar is
56	special except `'` itself (escaped by doubling), so colons, backticks, `#`,
57	em dashes and slashes are all safe:
58	
59	```yaml
60	description: 'Use when you build, review, or debug a FastAPI app: choosing def vs async def…'
61	```
62	
63	Rewording to drop the colon works too, but quoting is preferred: it preserves
64	the exact trigger wording, which is what drives skill selection.
65	
66	Verify with the same parser the CLI uses (`yaml` on npm):
67	
68	```bash
69	make lint-frontmatter                       # yq / PyYAML / js-yaml, whichever exists
70	./scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh --parser node skills   # exact npx-skills parity
71	```
72	
73	## Prevention
74	
75	- **`make lint-frontmatter`** (→ `skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh`)
76	  YAML-parses every `skills/**/SKILL.md`, checks that the root is a mapping with
77	  string `name` + `description`, and prints an actionable hint naming the file
78	  line to quote. Run it before publishing, alongside `make marketplace`.
79	- **`lint-skill.sh` now delegates to it** for the single-skill case, so the
80	  permissive awk extractor can no longer greenlight a file that real parsers
81	  reject.
82	- **Enforced twice**: `.github/workflows/validate.yml` runs the gate on push
83	  and PR (pinning the npm `yaml` package so CI agrees with the CLI rather than
84	  with the runner's `yq`), and `make install-hooks` puts the same
85	  `make validate` in a local `pre-push` hook.
86	- Other plain-scalar hazards the linter also flags, because they are the same
87	  class of bug:
88	  - `description: Do X # not Y` → YAML starts a **comment** at ` #` and
89	    silently truncates the description. This one *parses*, so it is a warning,
90	    not an error, and it is the more dangerous variant: the skill installs with
91	    a quietly shortened trigger string.
92	  - A value starting with a reserved character (`- ? , [ ] { } # & * ! | > % @ \``).
93	- Rule of thumb when authoring: **if a description contains `:`, `#`, or starts
94	  with punctuation, quote the whole value.**
95	
96	## Where this was hit
97	
98	Found 2026-07-27 when running
99	`npx skills add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills` and reading the warnings
100	above the picker. All 62 `skills/**/SKILL.md` files were then swept with both
101	`yq` and the npm `yaml` package; exactly those three failed, and both parsers
102	agreed. Fixed by single-quoting the three descriptions; the linter and this
103	doc were added in the same change.
104
```
</details></tool-use>

   578	            resolve_manifest_path(plugin_root, field, Some(path))
   579	                .map(|path| vec![path])
   580	                .unwrap_or_default()
   581	        }
   582	        Some(RawPluginManifestPaths::Paths(paths)) => paths
   583	            .iter()
   584	            .filter_map(|path| resolve_manifest_path(plugin_root, field, Some(path)))
   585	            .collect(),
   586	        Some(RawPluginManifestPaths::Invalid(value)) => {

   597	fn resolve_manifest_path(
   598	    plugin_root: &PathUri,
   599	    field: &'static str,
   600	    path: Option<&str>,
   601	) -> Option<PathUri> {
   602	    let path = path?;
   603	    if path.is_empty() {
   604	        return None;
   605	    }

   607	        tracing::warn!("ignoring {field}: path must start with `./` relative to plugin root");

   609	    };
   610	    if relative_path.is_empty() {
   611	        tracing::warn!("ignoring {field}: path must not be `./`");
   612	        return None;
   613	    }
   614	
   615	    let convention = plugin_root.infer_path_convention();
   616	    let has_parent_component = match convention {
   617	        Some(PathConvention::Windows) => relative_path
   618	            .split(['/', '\\'])
   619	            .any(|component| component == ".."),
   620	        Some(PathConvention::Posix) | None => {
   621	            relative_path.split('/').any(|component| component == "..")
   622	        }
   623	    };
   624	    if has_parent_component {
   625	        tracing::warn!("ignoring {field}: path must not contain '..'");
   626	        return None;
   627	    }
   628	
   629	    let has_windows_root = convention == Some(PathConvention::Windows)
   630	        && (relative_path.starts_with('\\')

   634	        return None;

For Claude Code, the native bundle is broader than a skill: its manifest/catalog can carry commands, agents, skills, hooks, MCP and LSP configuration, while installation is scoped (`user`, `project`, or `local`) and materialized into Claude’s plugin cache. That cache boundary is why `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` and relative paths matter; a repository-relative script path that works before installation may break after copying. I’m now contrasting this with `npx skills`, which is a Vercel-maintained cross-agent copier/metadata tool rather than either vendor’s marketplace protocol.
