63	
64	## Vendor System
65	
66	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
67	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
68	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
69	
70	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA.
71	
72	Active series in this repo:
73	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
74	
75	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
76	
77	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
78	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
79	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
80	
81	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
82	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
83	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
84	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
85	  the `npx skills` CLI has no lockfile, so users who installed the old
86	  name won't auto-map on `npx skills update`.
87	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
88	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
89	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
90	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
91	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
92	
93	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
94	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.
95	
96	## Marketplace Catalog
97	
98	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
99	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
100	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
101	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
102	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
103	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
104	for the full mechanism.
105	
106	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
107	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
108	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
109	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
110	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>` or
111	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
112	
113	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
114	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
115	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
116	frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
117	repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
118	`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
119	`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
120	within-group caveat in
121	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).
122	
123	## SKILL.md Format
124	
125	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.
126	
127	## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)
128	
129	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
130	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
131	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
132	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
133	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
134	
135	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
136	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
137	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
138	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
139	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
140	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
141	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
142	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
143	
144	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
145	
146	```bash
147	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
148	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
149	
150	# …or remove them afterward
151	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
152	```
153	
154	## Project Memory Workflow
155	
156	### Long-term backlog -> `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
157	
158	When work is explicitly deferred, add it to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using the
159	fixed section order `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P?`, `Done`.
160	
161	- Active items must use `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
162	- `P?` items must use `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
163	- Non-trivial research should be linked as `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
164	
165	`TODO.md` is parsed by [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts/todo-kanban.sh), so
166	do not invent alternate headings, nested bullets, or ad hoc checkbox formats.
167	
168	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
169	
170	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
171	
172	   ```bash
173	   ./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
174	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
175	   # add --backlog to also scaffold backlog/<slug>.md
176	   ```
177	
178	   This inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane
179	   and re-runs the validator. Refuses to write a malformed entry.
180	
181	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
182	
183	   ```bash
184	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
185	   ```
186	
187	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox" or "clear inbox.md", run
188	   [`./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`](scripts/sweep-inbox.sh). It prompts for
189	   priority/effort/title/description per loose line and calls
190	   `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs that only
191	   formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
192	
193	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh in your
194	   head; run `make kanban` (or `./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`)
195	   afterwards to catch drift.
196	
197	#### Promote a TODO when implementing it
198	
199	When implementing a TODO item, in the same commit run:
200	
201	```bash
202	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"
203	```
204	
205	That moves the matched active item into `## Done` with the dated `Done`
206	syntax and re-validates the file. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists for the
207	item, also mark it as shipped (don't delete — keep it as historical record).
208	
209	Keep `## Done` as the recent history buffer. Prune it into `CHANGELOG.md` only
210	when it contains items from a previous calendar year or grows past 20 entries.
211	
212	### External skill / MCP / domain catalog -> `docs/catalog/`
213	
214	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
215	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
216	own conventions). It has three subareas:
217	
218	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
219	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
220	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
221	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
222	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
223	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
224	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
225	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
226	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
227	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
228	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
229	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
230	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
231	  status / license / last_verified`).
232	
233	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
234	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
235	
236	| Status | Meaning |
237	|---|---|
238	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
239	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
240	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
241	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
242	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
243	
244	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
245	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
246	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
247	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
248	
249	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
250	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
251	
252	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
253	
254	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
255	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
256	
257	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
258	2. The root cause
259	3. The workaround
260	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
261	
262	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
263	the explanation they do not know yet.
264
```

1	# Agent skill compatibility
2	
3	This page records the cross-agent `SKILL.md` constraints this repo targets.
4	The goal is practical portability across coding agents, not the broadest set
5	of optional product-specific extensions.
6	
7	## Baseline we target
8	
9	Use the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) as
10	the portable baseline:
11	
12	| Field | Repo policy |
13	|---|---|
14	| `name` | Required, 1-64 chars, lowercase letters/digits with single hyphen separators, no leading/trailing hyphen, no `--`, should match the skill directory |
15	| `description` | Required, 1-1024 chars, describes both what the skill does and when to use it |
16	| `SKILL.md` body | Keep under ~500 lines; move long detail into `references/` |
17	| Optional frontmatter | Allowed only when a target agent needs it; keep local skills portable by default |
18	
19	Description budget tiers used by `skill-author`:
20	
21	| Tier | Length | Meaning |
22	|---|---:|---|
23	| Green | 120-500 chars | Preferred for local skills: enough trigger surface without context bloat |
24	| Yellow | 501-900 chars | Valid, but context-heavy; move details to the body or references |
25	| Orange | 901-1024 chars | Valid, but close to hard loader limits |
26	| Red | >1024 chars | Invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned validators |
27	
28	Also make the first 60 characters useful. The `npx skills` installer truncates
29	picker hints to 60 characters, and Codex may shorten descriptions when the
30	installed skill list is large.
31	
32	## Agent notes
33	
34	| Tool | Preference / constraint | Link |
35	|---|---|---|
36	| Agent Skills spec | Defines the portable directory layout, frontmatter fields, 64-char `name`, 1024-char `description`, optional `scripts/`, `references/`, and `assets/`. | [Specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) |
37	| Codex | Starts with each skill's name, description, and path, then loads full `SKILL.md` only when selected. The initial skills list has a context budget; descriptions should be concise and front-loaded. Codex can use optional `agents/openai.yaml` for UI metadata and invocation policy. | [Codex skills docs](https://developers.openai.com/codex/skills/create-skill) |
38	| Claude Code | Follows the open standard and adds fields such as `when_to_use`, `disable-model-invocation`, `user-invocable`, `allowed-tools`, `context`, and `hooks`. It truncates combined `description`/`when_to_use` listing text at 1,536 chars. | [Claude Code skills docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) |
39	| Cursor | Uses `SKILL.md` skills with the same practical 64-char `name` and 1024-char `description` budget in its managed `create-skill` guidance. It also supports `disable-model-invocation` for explicit-only skills. | [Cursor skills docs](https://cursor.com/docs/skills) |
40	| OpenCode | Recognizes `.opencode/skills`, `.claude/skills`, and `.agents/skills`; only specific frontmatter fields are recognized, unknown fields are ignored. It enforces 1-64 char names and 1-1024 char descriptions. | [OpenCode Agent Skills](https://opencode.ai/docs/skills/) |
41	| `npx skills` | Installer/distributor. Reads `name` and `description` from `SKILL.md`, shows only a 60-char description hint in the picker, and uses `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` for grouping. | [npx skills metadata model](npx-skills-metadata.md) |
42	
43	## How this repo applies it
44	
45	- Local skills should keep `description` in the green tier unless there is a
46	  concrete trigger-coverage reason to go longer.
47	- `skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh` enforces the portable hard
48	  limits: hyphen-case names, 64-char names, and 1024-char descriptions. It also
49	  reports yellow/orange tier notes without failing strict mode.
50	- `skills/local/skill-author/assets/SKILL.md.template` tells new authors to
51	  target 120-500 chars and never exceed 1024.
52	- Detailed trigger examples belong in `SKILL.md` body or `references/`, not in
53	  an oversized frontmatter description.
54	- Product-specific metadata is acceptable when needed, but should be deliberate:
55	  prefer portable frontmatter for local skills, leave vendored upstream metadata
56	  intact, and document any target-agent-only field in the skill body.
57	
58	## Incident that set the policy
59	
60	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap` previously had a 1106-character frontmatter
61	`description`. Codex 0.128.0 skipped it as invalid because the description
62	exceeded 1024 characters. We shortened the description to 489 characters and
63	updated `skill-author` so future local skills are caught before install-time
64	loader failures.
65
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# Creating local skills
2	
3	A local skill is a custom-authored skill maintained in this repo under
4	[`skills/local/<skill-name>/`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local).
5	
6	## Scaffold a new skill
7	
8	Use the bundled scaffolder (recommended — seeds the full agentskills.io
9	best-practice layout and fans out the discovery symlinks for non-universal
10	agents):
11	
12	```bash
13	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
14	```
15	
16	The script picks one of three **placement scopes** by walking up from your
17	CWD; override with `--local` / `--project` / `--global` when intent isn't
18	obvious:
19	
20	| Scope | Trigger | Canonical dir | Symlinks created |
21	|---|---|---|---|
22	| **LOCAL** | `vendor.yaml` / `skills/local/` / `skills/.claude-plugin/` found | `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/` with `--vendor`) | `.agents/skills/<name>` + `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>` |
23	| **PROJECT** | `.git` found | `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents — Cursor/Codex/OpenCode/Warp — pick this up directly) | `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any non-universal agent dir already present at the repo root) |
24	| **GLOBAL** | neither anchor, or `--global` | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `~/.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any non-universal agent dir already present under `$HOME`) |
25	
26	This mirrors the placement contract of `npx skills add` (canonical content
27	in `.agents/skills/` + relative symlinks into each non-universal agent's
28	home), so a skill scaffolded here will be picked up by Claude Code,
29	Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Warp, etc. without any extra wiring. See
30	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](../reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
31	for the upstream mechanism.
32	
33	Alternative (just the SKILL.md skeleton, no symlinks, no `references/` /
34	`scripts/` / `assets/`):
35	
36	```bash
37	cd skills/local
38	npx skills@latest init [skill-name]
39	```
40	
41	This creates only `skills/local/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` with the required
42	YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`).
43	
44	Before writing the description, check the repo's
45	[Agent skill compatibility](../reference/agent-skill-compatibility.md) policy.
46	Local skills should target portable coding-agent limits: hyphen-case names
47	under 64 chars, descriptions under 1024 chars, and 120-500 chars preferred.
48	
49	## Required structure
50	
51	See [Conventions](../conventions.md) for the full layout rules. In short:
52	
53	- `SKILL.md` — required, lean (under ~500 lines).
54	- `assets/` — templates the skill copies into target projects.
55	- `scripts/` — executable helpers (Bash 3.2 compatible).
56	- `references/` — long-form material loaded on demand.
57	
58	## Author the SKILL.md following agentskills.io best practices
59	
60	The two highest-leverage rules from the
61	[agentskills.io best practices](https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/best-practices):
62	
63	1. **Procedures over declarations.** Tell the agent what to *do*, not what
64	   to *be*. A SKILL.md that says "follow these three steps" is much more
65	   reliable than one that says "be a careful and methodical helper".
66	2. **Defaults over menus.** Pick one workflow as the default; offer
67	   alternatives via flags or in `references/`. Letting the agent choose
68	   between three equivalent options at every step is a debugging nightmare.
69	
70	A third rule we apply in this repo:
71	
72	- **Bundle the workflow as a script if you can.** If the skill keeps asking
73	  the agent to perform the same multi-step procedure, write it as a shell
74	  script in `scripts/` and make the SKILL.md call the script. The
75	  [`project-knowledge-harness`](../skills/project-knowledge-harness.md)
76	  skill is the reference for this pattern.
77	
78	## Add a docs page
79	
80	Every local skill should also have a page under `docs/skills/<skill>.md`
81	that explains, for a human reader, what the skill is for, when it
82	triggers, and what it costs to use. The `SKILL.md` is the agent-facing
83	contract; the docs page is the human-facing pitch. Both are valuable.
84	
85	When you create the docs page, also link it from
86	[`docs/skills/index.md`](../skills/index.md) and from `mkdocs.yml`'s `nav:`
87	block at the repo root.
88	
89	## Test by installing into a scratch project
90	
91	```bash
92	mkdir /tmp/scratch && cd /tmp/scratch
93	git init
94	npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
95	```
96	
97	This pulls the new skill into `.agents/skills/` of a clean project so you
98	can verify the SKILL.md activates as you expect.
99
```

1	# This-repo conventions
2	
3	Conventions specific to the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repository. Skills
4	authored elsewhere may follow different rules; this file is the source of
5	truth for **this** repo.
6	
7	## Layout
8	
9	```
10	skills/
11	├── local/             # skills authored in this repo (committed in full)
12	│   └── <skill-name>/
13	│       ├── SKILL.md
14	│       ├── references/
15	│       ├── scripts/
16	│       └── assets/
17	└── vendor/            # skills cherry-picked from upstream repos
18	    └── <skill-name>/
19	        └── ...        # synced via scripts/sync-vendor.sh
20	```
21	
22	- **New skills authored here go in `skills/local/`.** Always.
23	- **Don't manually edit anything in `skills/vendor/`** — it gets overwritten by
24	  the next `make sync`. Upstream changes go through `vendor.yaml` + `make sync`.
25	- **`.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` at the repo root are active
26	  discovery-symlink farms**, not legacy. Each entry under them is a relative
27	  symlink (`../../skills/local/<name>` or `../../skills/vendor/<name>`) so
28	  that Cursor / Codex / Warp / OpenCode (`.agents/skills/`) and Claude Code
29	  (`.claude/skills/`) can dogfood the skills authored in this repo. The
30	  `new-skill.sh` scaffolder creates these symlinks automatically in **LOCAL
31	  mode**; never add new *canonical* skill content directly under them here.
32	
33	## `new-skill.sh` placement scopes
34	
35	`scripts/new-skill.sh` supports three placement scopes that mirror the
36	behavior of `npx skills add` (`vercel-labs/skills`). Auto-detection
37	precedence (when no flag given):
38	
39	1. **LOCAL** — publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml`, `skills/local/`, or
40	   `skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) found walking up. This is the
41	   default *inside this very repo*. Canonical content lives in
42	   `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with
43	   `--vendor`); the script adds the `.agents/skills/` + `.claude/skills/`
44	   discovery symlinks for you.
45	2. **PROJECT** — a git root found walking up. Canonical content goes to
46	   `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents like Cursor / Codex /
47	   OpenCode / Warp / Gemini-CLI / Copilot read this directly); a relative
48	   symlink `<repo>/.claude/skills/<name> -> ../../.agents/skills/<name>` is
49	   added for Claude Code, plus links for any other non-universal agent dir
50	   (e.g. `.windsurf/`, `.continue/`) that already exists at the repo root.
51	3. **GLOBAL** — neither anchor found, or `--global` forced. Same shape as
52	   PROJECT but rooted at `$HOME`: canonical at `~/.agents/skills/<name>/`,
53	   plus `~/.claude/skills/<name>` and any other already-present
54	   `~/.<agent>/skills/` link.
55	
56	The fan-out rule is "claude-code always, others only if their config root
57	already exists at the base dir" — this mirrors `npx skills add`'s
58	"don't create `.windsurf/` unless the project already uses Windsurf"
59	behavior. The script never creates a new top-level agent home dir.
60	
61	Symlinks are always *relative* with a fixed `../../` prefix because both
62	the link's parent (`.../skills/`) and the canonical dir
63	(`.../.agents/skills/` or `.../skills/local/`) are exactly two levels under
64	the base dir. See [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md)
65	for the historical bug this convention prevents.
66	
67	## Skill discovery
68	
69	The `skills` CLI looks for `SKILL.md` files like this:
70	
71	1. **First pass:** one level deep — `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
72	2. **Fallback:** recursive up to **5 levels** if first pass found nothing
73	   useful.
74	
75	That's why `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` and `skills/vendor/<name>/SKILL.md`
76	both work — they're 2 levels deep, well within the recursive fallback. **Don't
77	nest a skill more than 5 levels deep** or it becomes invisible.
78	
79	## Scripts naming and mirroring
80	
81	Some scripts are bundled into a skill **and** mirrored to `scripts/` at repo
82	root. The pattern:
83	
84	| Canonical location | Mirror |
85	|---|---|
86	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/add-todo.sh` | `scripts/add-todo.sh` |
87	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` | `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` |
88	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/promote-todo.sh` | `scripts/promote-todo.sh` |
89	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/todo-kanban.sh` | `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` |
90	
91	Reason: the canonical copy travels with the skill (downstream consumers get it
92	via `init.sh`). The root-level mirror is for *this* repo's own use so `make`
93	targets and CI don't have to know the skill's path.
94	
95	**Mirrors must stay byte-identical.** If you edit one, run the equivalent
96	`cp` to update the other and verify with `diff`. There is currently no
97	automated check for this — be careful.
98	
99	## Documentation
100	
101	- `README.md` — short repo entrypoint with install snippet.
102	- `docs/` — built into a MkDocs Material site at
103	  `https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/`.
104	- `docs/skills/<skill-name>.md` — user-facing docs for each local skill. Link
105	  back to the canonical SKILL.md on GitHub via absolute URL (see linking rules
106	  in `docs/reference/docs-stack-recipe.md`).
107	
108	When you add a new local skill, also add:
109	
110	1. A row to `docs/skills/index.md`.
111	2. A `docs/skills/<skill-name>.md` page (can be short; cross-link to SKILL.md).
112	3. A nav entry in `mkdocs.yml`.
113	4. A row to the README's "What's in here" table.
114	
115	## Project memory
116	
117	This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` skill on itself. That means:
118	
119	- `TODO.md` is structured (P1/P2/P3/P?/Done sections, validated by
120	  `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`).
121	- `backlog/inbox.md` is the loose-capture inbox.
122	- `backlog/<slug>.md` holds research notes for non-trivial items.
123	- `pitfalls/<slug>.md` holds debugging traps with symptom-first titles.
124	
125	When authoring a skill, if you discover a non-obvious trap, write it to
126	`pitfalls/`. Don't bury it in commit messages or chat history.
127	
128	## AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md
129	
130	`AGENTS.md` is a **symlink** to `CLAUDE.md`. Edit either one. Don't replace
131	the symlink with a real file or they'll drift.
132	
133	## Bash compatibility
134	
135	All bundled scripts must be **bash 3.2 compatible** (stock macOS). See
136	`script-design.md` § "Bash 3.2 compatibility" for the safe subset and
137	escape hatches.
138	
139	## When this repo's conventions conflict with agentskills.io
140	
141	The agentskills.io best practices are upstream / generic; this file is local /
142	specific. When they conflict, this file wins **for skills authored in this
143	repo**. Notable specifics:
144	
145	- We default to bundling helper scripts in `scripts/` rather than relying on
146	  ad-hoc `uvx` invocations, because we want the helpers to compose with the
147	  repo's `Makefile` and CI.
148	- We use Bash for orchestration scripts (TODO management, vendor sync) so they
149	  run without a Python environment. PEP 723 Python is fine for analytical or
150	  parsing-heavy helpers.
151	- Skill descriptions in this repo lean **even pushier** than the agentskills.io
152	  guidance because we're optimizing for the OpenCode/Claude Code default
153	  triggering behavior, which under-triggers more aggressively than Claude.ai.
154

476	    printf '"%s"' "$(printf '%s' "$line" | sed 's/"/\\"/g')"
477	  done <<EOF
478	$SYMLINKS_CREATED
479	EOF
480	  printf ']'
481	}
482	
483	NEXT_STEPS="\"Edit $CANONICAL_DIR/SKILL.md to fill in description and workflow\",\"Run lint-skill.sh $CANONICAL_DIR to verify\""
484	
485	printf '{"skill":"%s","mode":"%s","canonical":"%s","symlinks":%s,"next_steps":[%s]}\n' \
486	  "$NAME" "$MODE" "$CANONICAL_DIR" "$(json_symlinks)" "$NEXT_STEPS"

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# lint-frontmatter.sh — Validate SKILL.md YAML frontmatter across a whole tree.
3	#
4	# Why this exists: every agent harness (`npx skills`, Claude Code, Cursor,
5	# Codex) parses SKILL.md frontmatter with a real YAML parser and **silently
6	# skips** any skill whose frontmatter fails to parse. `lint-skill.sh` reads
7	# frontmatter with a permissive awk extractor, so it happily passes files
8	# that real parsers reject. This script closes that gap.
9	#
10	# The trap that motivated it — an unquoted `description:` containing ": ":
11	#
12	#   description: Use when you debug a FastAPI app: choosing def vs async def
13	#                                                ^ YAML reads a nested mapping
14	#     npx skills → "YAML parse error: Nested mappings are not allowed in
15	#                   compact mappings"
16	#
17	# Fix: wrap the value in single quotes.
18	#
19	# Checks per SKILL.md:
20	#   1. Frontmatter delimiters — `---` on line 1, closing `---` below it
21	#   2. Frontmatter parses as YAML (yq / PyYAML / js-yaml, whichever is found)
22	#   3. Root is a mapping; `name` and `description` present as plain strings
23	#   4. (warn) unquoted plain scalar containing " #" — YAML treats the rest of
24	#      the line as a comment and silently truncates the value
25	#
26	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS). No hard dependency: with no YAML parser
27	# on PATH it degrades to the pattern heuristic and says so.
28	
29	set -uo pipefail
30	
31	usage() {
32	  cat <<'EOF'
33	Usage: lint-frontmatter.sh [OPTIONS] [PATH...]
34	
35	Validate the YAML frontmatter of every SKILL.md under PATH (default: ".").
36	PATH may be a SKILL.md file or a directory to search recursively.
37	
38	Options:
39	  --parser NAME      Force a parser: auto (default), yq, python3 (PyYAML),
40	                     node (the js "yaml" package — what `npx skills` uses).
41	  --quiet            Only print failures and the summary line.
42	  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.
43	
44	Examples:
45	  bash lint-frontmatter.sh                    # lint every SKILL.md under cwd
46	  bash lint-frontmatter.sh skills             # lint a collection directory
47	  bash lint-frontmatter.sh skills/local/my-skill/SKILL.md
48	
49	Exit codes:
50	  0  every SKILL.md parses and has string name + description
51	  1  at least one file failed
52	  2  invalid arguments / path not found / forced parser unavailable
53	EOF
54	}
55	
56	QUIET=0
57	FORCED_PARSER="auto"
58	PATHS=()
59	
60	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
61	  case "$1" in
62	    --parser)  [ $# -ge 2 ] || { printf 'error: --parser needs a value (auto|yq|python3|node)\n' >&2; exit 2; }
63	               FORCED_PARSER="$2"; shift 2 ;;
64	    --parser=*) FORCED_PARSER="${1#--parser=}"; shift ;;
65	    --quiet)   QUIET=1; shift ;;
66	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
67	    -*)        printf 'error: unknown flag: %s (try --help)\n' "$1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
68	    *)         PATHS+=("$1"); shift ;;
69	  esac
70	done
71	
72	[ ${#PATHS[@]} -eq 0 ] && PATHS=(".")
73	
74	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
75	# Parser detection — prefer the strictest thing available.
76	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
77	PARSER="none"
78	case "$FORCED_PARSER" in
79	  auto) ;;
80	  yq)      command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf 'error: yq not found on PATH\n' >&2; exit 2; }; PARSER="yq" ;;
81	  python3) python3 -c 'import yaml' >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf 'error: python3 with PyYAML not available\n' >&2; exit 2; }; PARSER="python3" ;;
82	  node)    node -e "require('yaml')" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf 'error: node with the "yaml" package not available (try NODE_PATH=...)\n' >&2; exit 2; }; PARSER="node" ;;
83	  *)       printf 'error: unknown --parser: %s (auto|yq|python3|node)\n' "$FORCED_PARSER" >&2; exit 2 ;;
84	esac
85	
86	if [ "$PARSER" = "none" ]; then
87	  if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
88	    PARSER="yq"
89	  elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && python3 -c 'import yaml' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
90	    PARSER="python3"
91	  elif command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 && node -e "require('yaml')" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
92	    PARSER="node"
93	  fi
94	fi
95	
96	# probe_* contract: print one line to stdout, either
97	#   OK|<root_type>|<name_type>|<desc_type>     types: map/str/null/other
98	#   FAIL|<first line of the parser error>
99	# Parser errors point at the extracted frontmatter (and, for yq, at the temp
100	# file). Drop the temp path and shift line numbers by 1 so they name the line
101	# in SKILL.md itself.
102	normalize_err() {
103	  sed -e "s|^Error: bad file '[^']*': ||" -e 's| in "[^"]*"||' | awk '
104	    {
105	      out = ""; s = $0
106	      while (match(s, /line [0-9]+/)) {
107	        n = substr(s, RSTART + 5, RLENGTH - 5) + 1
108	        out = out substr(s, 1, RSTART - 1) "line " n
109	        s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH)
110	      }
111	      print out s
112	    }'
113	}
114	
115	probe_yq() {
116	  local tmp="$1" err root name desc
117	  if ! err=$(yq e '.' "$tmp" 2>&1 >/dev/null); then
118	    printf 'FAIL|%s\n' "$(printf '%s' "$err" | head -n1)"
119	    return
120	  fi
121	  root=$(yq e '. | tag' "$tmp" 2>/dev/null)
122	  name=$(yq e '.name | tag' "$tmp" 2>/dev/null)
123	  desc=$(yq e '.description | tag' "$tmp" 2>/dev/null)
124	  printf 'OK|%s|%s|%s\n' \
125	    "$(normalize_tag "$root")" "$(normalize_tag "$name")" "$(normalize_tag "$desc")"
126	}
127	
128	normalize_tag() {
129	  case "$1" in
130	    '!!map') printf 'map' ;;
131	    '!!str') printf 'str' ;;
132	    '!!null'|'') printf 'null' ;;
133	    *) printf 'other' ;;
134	  esac
135	}
136	
137	probe_python3() {
138	  python3 - "$1" <<'PY'
139	import sys, yaml
140	def t(v):
141	    if v is None: return "null"
142	    if isinstance(v, str): return "str"
143	    if isinstance(v, dict): return "map"
144	    return "other"
145	try:
146	    with open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8") as fh:
147	        doc = yaml.safe_load(fh)
148	except Exception as exc:
149	    print("FAIL|" + str(exc).replace("\n", " ")[:200])
150	    sys.exit(0)
151	if isinstance(doc, dict):
152	    print("OK|map|%s|%s" % (t(doc.get("name")), t(doc.get("description"))))
153	else:
154	    print("OK|%s|null|null" % t(doc))
155	PY
156	}
157	
158	probe_node() {
159	  node -e '
160	    const YAML = require("yaml"), fs = require("fs");
161	    const t = v => v === null || v === undefined ? "null"
162	      : typeof v === "string" ? "str"
163	      : (typeof v === "object" && !Array.isArray(v)) ? "map" : "other";
164	    let doc;
165	    try { doc = YAML.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8")); }
166	    catch (e) { console.log("FAIL|" + String(e.message).split("\n")[0].slice(0, 200)); process.exit(0); }
167	    if (t(doc) === "map") console.log(`OK|map|${t(doc.name)}|${t(doc.description)}`);
168	    else console.log(`OK|${t(doc)}|null|null`);
169	  ' "$1"
170	}
171	
172	probe() {
173	  local raw
174	  case "$PARSER" in
175	    yq)      raw=$(probe_yq "$1") ;;
176	    python3) raw=$(probe_python3 "$1") ;;
177	    node)    raw=$(probe_node "$1") ;;
178	    *)       raw='SKIP|no YAML parser on PATH' ;;
179	  esac
180	  case "$raw" in
181	    FAIL\|*) printf 'FAIL|%s\n' "$(printf '%s' "${raw#FAIL|}" | normalize_err)" ;;
182	    *)       printf '%s\n' "$raw" ;;
183	  esac
184	}
185	
186	# Pattern heuristic: flag unquoted top-level plain scalars that YAML will
187	# either reject or silently mangle. Prints "reason" lines. Used as the hint
188	# when a parse fails, and as the only check when no parser is installed.
189	risky_scalars() {
190	  awk '
191	    /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+:[ \t]+[^ \t]/ {
192	      key = $0; sub(/:.*/, "", key)
193	      val = $0; sub(/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+:[ \t]*/, "", val)
194	      sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", val)
195	      first = substr(val, 1, 1)
196	      # Quoted or block scalars are already safe.
197	      if (first == "\"" || first == "'\''" || first == ">" || first == "|" \
198	          || first == "[" || first == "{") next
199	      if (val ~ /: / || val ~ /:$/)
200	        printf "  line %d: %s value contains \": \" — YAML reads it as a nested mapping; wrap the value in single quotes\n", NR + 1, key
201	      else if (val ~ / #/)
202	        printf "  line %d: %s value contains \" #\" — YAML starts a comment there and silently truncates the value; wrap it in single quotes\n", NR + 1, key
203	      else if (index("-?,[]{}#&*!|>%@`", first) > 0)
204	        printf "  line %d: %s value starts with the reserved YAML character %s — wrap the value in single quotes\n", NR + 1, key, first
205	    }
206	  ' "$1"
207	}
208	
209	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
210	# Collect SKILL.md files
211	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
212	collect() {
213	  local p
214	  for p in "$@"; do
215	    if [ -f "$p" ]; then
216	      printf '%s\n' "$p"
217	    elif [ -d "$p" ]; then
218	      find "$p" -name SKILL.md \
219	        -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
220	        -not -path '*/.git/*' \
221	        -not -path '*/site/*' 2>/dev/null
222	    else
223	      printf 'error: no such file or directory: %s\n' "$p" >&2
224	      exit 2
225	    fi
226	  done | sort -u
227	}
228	
229	FILES=$(collect "${PATHS[@]}") || exit 2
230	if [ -z "$FILES" ]; then
231	  printf 'error: no SKILL.md found under: %s\n' "${PATHS[*]}" >&2
232	  exit 2
233	fi
234	
235	TMP=$(mktemp -t skill-frontmatter.XXXXXX) || exit 2
236	trap 'rm -f "$TMP"' EXIT
237	
238	CHECKED=0
239	FAILED=0
240	WARNED=0
241	
242	say()  { [ "$QUIET" = "1" ] || printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
243	fail() { printf 'FAIL  %s\n' "$1"; shift; [ $# -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "$@"; FAILED=$((FAILED + 1)); }
244	
245	while IFS= read -r file; do
246	  [ -n "$file" ] || continue
247	  CHECKED=$((CHECKED + 1))
248	
249	  # 1. Delimiters
250	  if [ "$(head -n1 "$file" | tr -d '\r')" != "---" ]; then
251	    fail "$file" "  no opening '---' on line 1 (frontmatter is missing)"
252	    continue
253	  fi
254	  close=$(awk 'NR>1 && /^---[ \t]*\r?$/ {print NR; exit}' "$file")
255	  if [ -z "$close" ]; then
256	    fail "$file" "  no closing '---' below the opening delimiter"
257	    continue
258	  fi
259	  sed -n "2,$((close - 1))p" "$file" > "$TMP"
260	
261	  # 2-3. Parse + required string fields
262	  result=$(probe "$TMP")
263	  status=${result%%|*}
264	  rest=${result#*|}
265	
266	  case "$status" in
267	    FAIL)
268	      hints=$(risky_scalars "$TMP")
269	      if [ -n "$hints" ]; then
270	        fail "$file" "  YAML parse error: $rest" "$hints"
271	      else
272	        fail "$file" "  YAML parse error: $rest"
273	      fi
274	      continue
275	      ;;
276	    SKIP)
277	      hints=$(risky_scalars "$TMP")
278	      if [ -n "$hints" ]; then
279	        fail "$file" "$hints"
280	      else
281	        say "ok    $file (heuristic only — no YAML parser on PATH)"
282	      fi
283	      continue
284	      ;;
285	  esac
286	
287	  root=${rest%%|*}; rest=${rest#*|}
288	  name_t=${rest%%|*}; desc_t=${rest#*|}
289	
290	  if [ "$root" != "map" ]; then
291	    fail "$file" "  frontmatter is not a YAML mapping (parsed as: $root)"
292	    continue
293	  fi
294	
295	  problems=""
296	  [ "$name_t" = "str" ] || problems="$problems
297	  'name' must be a string (got: $name_t)"
298	  [ "$desc_t" = "str" ] || problems="$problems
299	  'description' must be a string (got: $desc_t)"
300	
301	  if [ -n "$problems" ]; then
302	    fail "$file" "${problems#
303	}"
304	    continue
305	  fi
306	
307	  # 4. Silent-truncation warning (parses fine, but loses text).
308	  warnings=$(risky_scalars "$TMP" | grep -- 'silently truncates' || true)
309	  if [ -n "$warnings" ]; then
310	    printf 'WARN  %s\n%s\n' "$file" "$warnings"
311	    WARNED=$((WARNED + 1))
312	  else
313	    say "ok    $file"
314	  fi
315	done <<EOF
316	$FILES
317	EOF
318	
319	say ""
320	printf 'checked %d SKILL.md (parser: %s) — %d failed, %d warned\n' \
321	  "$CHECKED" "$PARSER" "$FAILED" "$WARNED"
322	
323	if [ "$PARSER" = "none" ]; then
324	  printf 'note: no YAML parser found (install yq, PyYAML, or the js "yaml" package) — pattern heuristic only\n' >&2
325	fi
326	
327	[ "$FAILED" -gt 0 ] && exit 1
328	exit 0
329
```

```text
# Plugin JSON sample spec

```json
{
  "name": "plugin-name",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "description": "Brief plugin description",
  "author": {
    "name": "Author Name",
    "email": "author@example.com",
    "url": "https://github.com/author"
  },
  "homepage": "https://docs.example.com/plugin",
  "repository": "https://github.com/author/plugin",
  "license": "MIT",
  "keywords": ["keyword1", "keyword2"],
  "skills": "./skills/",
  "hooks": "./hooks.json",
  "mcpServers": "./.mcp.json",
  "apps": "./.app.json",
  "interface": {
    "displayName": "Plugin Display Name",
    "shortDescription": "Short description for subtitle",
    "longDescription": "Long description for details page",
    "developerName": "OpenAI",
    "category": "Productivity",
    "capabilities": ["Interactive", "Write"],
    "websiteURL": "https://openai.com/",
    "privacyPolicyURL": "https://openai.com/policies/row-privacy-policy/",
    "termsOfServiceURL": "https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/",
    "defaultPrompt": [
      "Summarize my inbox and draft replies for me.",
      "Find open bugs and turn them into Linear tickets.",
      "Review today's meetings and flag scheduling gaps."
    ],
    "brandColor": "#3B82F6",
    "composerIcon": "./assets/icon.png",
    "logo": "./assets/logo.png",
    "logoDark": "./assets/logo-dark.png",
    "screenshots": [
      "./assets/screenshot1.png",
      "./assets/screenshot2.png",
      "./assets/screenshot3.png"
    ]
  }
}
```

## Field guide

### Top-level fields

- `name` (`string`): Plugin identifier (kebab-case, no spaces). Required if `plugin.json` is provided and used as manifest name and component namespace.
- `version` (`string`): Plugin semantic version.
- `description` (`string`): Short purpose summary.
- `author` (`object`): Publisher identity.
  - `name` (`string`): Author or team name.
  - `email` (`string`): Contact email.
  - `url` (`string`): Author/team homepage or profile URL.
- `homepage` (`string`): Documentation URL for plugin usage.
- `repository` (`string`): Source code URL.
- `license` (`string`): License identifier (for example `MIT`, `Apache-2.0`).
- `keywords` (`array` of `string`): Search/discovery tags.
- `skills` (`string`): Relative path to skill directories/files.
- `hooks` (`string`): Hook config path.
- `mcpServers` (`string` or `object`): MCP config path, or an object whose keys are MCP server names and whose values are MCP server config objects.
- `apps` (`string`): App manifest path for plugin integrations.
- `interface` (`object`): Interface/UX metadata block for plugin presentation.

`mcpServers` may be declared as a companion file path:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": "./.mcp.json"
}
```

Or as an object directly in `plugin.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "counter": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://sample.example/counter/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

### `interface` fields

- `displayName` (`string`): User-facing title shown for the plugin.
- `shortDescription` (`string`): Brief subtitle used in compact views.
- `longDescription` (`string`): Longer description used on details screens.
- `developerName` (`string`): Human-readable publisher name.
- `category` (`string`): Plugin category bucket.
- `capabilities` (`array` of `string`): Capability list from implementation.
- `websiteURL` (`string`): Public website for the plugin.
- `privacyPolicyURL` (`string`): Privacy policy URL.
- `termsOfServiceURL` (`string`): Terms of service URL.
- `defaultPrompt` (`array` of `string`): Starter prompts shown in composer/UX context.
  - Include at most 3 strings. Entries after the first 3 are ignored and will not be included.
  - Each string is capped at 128 characters. Longer entries are truncated.
  - Prefer short starter prompts around 50 characters so they scan well in the UI.
- `brandColor` (`string`): Theme color for the plugin card.
- `composerIcon` (`string`): Path to icon asset.
- `logo` (`string`): Path to logo asset.
- `logoDark` (`string`): Optional path to the logo asset used in dark mode.
- `screenshots` (`array` of `string`): List of screenshot asset paths.
  - Screenshot entries must be PNG filenames and stored under `./assets/`.
  - Keep file paths relative to plugin root.

### Path conventions and defaults

- Path values should be relative and begin with `./`.
- `skills`, `hooks`, and string-valued `mcpServers` are supplemented on top of default component discovery; they do not replace defaults.
- Custom path values must follow the plugin root convention and naming/namespacing rules.
- This repo’s scaffold writes `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`; treat that as the manifest location this skill generates.

# Marketplace JSON sample spec

`marketplace.json` depends on where the plugin should live. New plugin creation defaults to the
personal marketplace unless the caller explicitly requests a repo-local destination:

- Personal plugin: `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`
- Repo/team plugin: `<repo-root>/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`

```json
{
  "name": "openai-curated",
  "interface": {
    "displayName": "ChatGPT Official"
  },
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "linear",
      "source": {
        "source": "local",
        "path": "./plugins/linear"
      },
      "policy": {
        "installation": "AVAILABLE",
        "authentication": "ON_INSTALL"
      },
      "category": "Productivity"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Marketplace field guide

### Top-level fields

- `name` (`string`): Marketplace identifier or catalog name.
- `interface` (`object`, optional): Marketplace presentation metadata.
- `plugins` (`array`): Ordered plugin entries. This order determines how Codex renders plugins.

### `interface` fields

- `displayName` (`string`, optional): User-facing marketplace title.

### Plugin entry fields

- `name` (`string`): Plugin identifier. Match the plugin folder name and `plugin.json` `name`.
- `source` (`object`): Plugin source descriptor.
  - `source` (`string`): Use `local` for this repo workflow.
  - `path` (`string`): Relative plugin path based on the marketplace root.
    - Personal plugin in `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`: `./plugins/<plugin-name>`
    - Repo/team plugin: `./plugins/<plugin-name>`
  - The same relative path convention is used for both personal and repo/team marketplaces.
    - Example: with `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, `./plugins/<plugin-name>` resolves to
      `~/plugins/<plugin-name>`.
- `policy` (`object`): Marketplace policy block. Always include it.
  - `installation` (`string`): Availability policy.
    - Allowed values: `NOT_AVAILABLE`, `AVAILABLE`, `INSTALLED_BY_DEFAULT`
    - Default for new entries: `AVAILABLE`
  - `authentication` (`string`): Authentication timing policy.
    - Allowed values: `ON_INSTALL`, `ON_USE`
    - Default for new entries: `ON_INSTALL`
  - `products` (`array` of `string`, optional): Product override for this plugin entry. Omit it unless product gating is explicitly requested.
- `category` (`string`): Display category bucket. Always include it.

### Marketplace generation rules

- `displayName` belongs under the top-level `interface` object, not individual plugin entries.
- When creating a new marketplace file from scratch, seed `interface.displayName` alongside top-level `name`.
- Always include `policy.installation`, `policy.authentication`, and `category` on every generated or updated plugin entry.
- Treat `policy.products` as an override and omit it unless explicitly requested.
- Append new entries unless the user explicitly requests reordering.
- Replace an existing entry for the same plugin only when overwrite is intentional.
- Default new plugin creation to the personal marketplace.
- Use a repo/team marketplace only when the user specifically requests that destination.
- Only override the marketplace `name` when the default `personal` name is already taken or
  installed and you need to seed a different new marketplace file.
- Choose marketplace location to match the selected destination:
  - Personal plugin: `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`
  - Repo/team plugin: `<repo-root>/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`

### Plugin validation notes

- The validator mirrors the workspace plugin ingestion schema so generated plugins follow the same
  manifest contract from the start.
- Plugin manifests must include real values for `name`, `version`, `description`,
  `author.name`, and the required `interface` fields.
- `version` must use strict semver.
- `websiteURL`, `privacyPolicyURL`, and `termsOfServiceURL` must be absolute `https://` URLs when
  present.
- `composerIcon`, `logo`, `logoDark`, and `screenshots` must point to real files inside the plugin archive when
  present.
- `apps` should appear in `plugin.json` only when `.app.json` actually exists.
- `mcpServers` may point to `.mcp.json` or contain the MCP server object directly in
  `plugin.json`.
- Validation rejects unsupported manifest fields such as `hooks`, so the scaffold keeps them out of
  generated manifests.
- Run `scripts/validate_plugin.py <plugin-path>` before handing back a generated plugin. It adds one
  intentional preflight check that rejects leftover `[TODO: ...]` placeholders.
```
</details></tool-use>

13	# (or pin a commit SHA in `rev:`) so an unrelated skill's tag can't silently
14	# bump this hook.

# Plugins

This repository contains a curated collection of Codex plugin examples.

Each plugin lives under `plugins/<name>/` with a required
`.codex-plugin/plugin.json` manifest and optional companion surfaces such as
`skills/`, `.app.json`, `.mcp.json`, plugin-level `agents/`, `commands/`,
`hooks.json`, `assets/`, and other supporting files.

The default marketplace lives at `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and points
at the standard `plugins/` directory. API key login users have a separate
marketplace at `.agents/plugins/api_marketplace.json`.

Highlighted richer examples in this repo include:

- `plugins/figma` for `use_figma`, Code to Canvas, Code Connect, and design system rules
- `plugins/notion` for planning, research, meetings, and knowledge capture
- `plugins/build-ios-apps` for SwiftUI implementation, refactors, performance, and debugging
- `plugins/build-macos-apps` for macOS SwiftUI/AppKit workflows, build/run/debug loops, and packaging guidance
- `plugins/build-web-apps` for deployment, UI, payments, and database workflows
- `plugins/expo` for Expo and React Native apps, SDK upgrades, EAS workflows, and Codex Run actions
- `plugins/netlify`, `plugins/remotion`, and `plugins/google-slides` for additional public skill- and MCP-backed plugin bundles
```

## Snapshot

Inspected `main` at commit [`3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d`](https://github.com/lencx/skills/commit/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d), dated 2026-08-12. The complete pinned [repository tree](https://github.com/lencx/skills/tree/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d) contains no `.github` workflows, `package.json`, release configuration, or separate installation document; installation is documented only in `README.md`.

The manifests declare version `1.4.0`. The annotated [`v1.4.0`](https://github.com/lencx/skills/releases/tag/v1.4.0) tag points to commit `388116ee866a2098c96c8a069df90bd8bcae3169`; current `main` is one commit ahead, with only `README.md` changed in that commit. There are currently no GitHub Releases or release assets.

## Manifest behavior

### `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`

[Source, lines 1–21](https://github.com/lencx/skills/blob/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json#L1-L21)

- Defines a marketplace named `lencx`, including publisher identity and URL.
- Registers exactly one plugin, `lencx-skills`.
- `"source": "./"` makes the repository root the plugin source.
- Adds discovery metadata: description, `development` category, and three keywords.
- It carries no version itself; versioning comes from the plugin manifest.

This mapping explains the install identifier `lencx-skills@lencx`: plugin name followed by marketplace name.

### `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`

[Source, lines 1–19](https://github.com/lencx/skills/blob/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d/.claude-plugin/plugin.json#L1-L19)

- Explicitly references the SchemaStore Claude Code plugin schema.
- Declares plugin name `lencx-skills`, version `1.4.0`, author, homepage, repository, MIT license, and keywords.
- `"skills": "./skills/"` exposes the repository’s checked-in `skills/` directory.
- Declares no commands, agents, hooks, MCP servers, or executable setup behavior. It is a skills-only plugin manifest.

### `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`

[Source, lines 1–37](https://github.com/lencx/skills/blob/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d/.codex-plugin/plugin.json#L1-L37)

- Repeats the core identity and version metadata from the Claude manifest.
- Also points `"skills"` at `./skills/`.
- Adds a Codex-specific `interface` section containing:
  - display, short, and long descriptions;
  - developer and category;
  - two advertised capabilities;
  - website URL;
  - two suggested/default prompts;
  - brand color;
  - `composerIcon` and `logo`, both resolving to root `icon.svg`.
- It has no `$schema` declaration and no executable behavior.
- There is no separate `.codex-plugin/marketplace.json`; repository discovery is driven by the Codex marketplace command and this plugin manifest.

## Packaging script

[`scripts/package-codex-plugin.sh`, lines 1–53](https://github.com/lencx/skills/blob/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d/scripts/package-codex-plugin.sh#L1-L53)

Exact behavior:

1. Enables Bash strict mode with `set -euo pipefail` ([lines 1–3](https://github.com/lencx/skills/blob/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d/scripts/package-codex-plugin.sh#L1-L3)).
2. Resolves its physical directory and repository root independently of the caller’s working directory ([lines 5–6](https://github.com/lencx/skills/blob/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d/scripts/package-codex-plugin.sh#L5-L6)).
3. Uses its first argument as the output directory, defaulting to repository-root `dist/` ([line 7](https://github.com/lencx/skills/blob/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d/scripts/package-codex-plugin.sh#L7)). A relative explicit argument is relative to the caller’s current directory.
4. Fails if `zip` is unavailable ([lines 9–12](https://github.com/lencx/skills/blob/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d/scripts/package-codex-plugin.sh#L9-L12)).
5. Fails if any of these are missing:
   - `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`
   - `icon.svg`
   - `skills/`
   - `LICENSE`
   - `README.md`  
   ([lines 14–27](https://github.com/lencx/skills/blob/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d/scripts/package-codex-plugin.sh#L14-L27)).
6. Creates and canonicalizes the output directory, then creates a temporary directory ([lines 29–32](https://github.com/lencx/skills/blob/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d/scripts/package-codex-plugin.sh#L29-L32)).
7. Registers an `EXIT` trap that removes the temporary directory ([lines 34–39](https://github.com/lencx/skills/blob/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d/scripts/package-codex-plugin.sh#L34-L39)).
8. Recursively and quietly creates `lencx-skills-codex.zip`, containing only:
   - `.codex-plugin/`
   - `icon.svg`
   - `skills/`
   - `LICENSE`
   - `README.md`  
   It excludes `.DS_Store` and `__MACOSX` metadata ([lines 41–50](https://github.com/lencx/skills/blob/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d/scripts/package-codex-plugin.sh#L41-L50)).
9. Force-replaces any destination archive with the same unversioned filename and prints its canonical output path ([lines 52–53](https://github.com/lencx/skills/blob/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d/scripts/package-codex-plugin.sh#L52-L53)).

The archive deliberately omits `.claude-plugin/`, the packaging script, and other repository files.

The temporary directory is deleted on script exit. No generated ZIP is committed or attached to a GitHub Release.

## User installation paths

The README warns users to choose either the generic skills installer or a native plugin because using both exposes every skill twice ([lines 17–19](https://github.com/lencx/skills/blob/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d/README.md#L17-L19)).

### Generic skills installer

Recommended automatic install:

```bash
npx skills@latest add lencx/skills
```

[README lines 21–25](https://github.com/lencx/skills/blob/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d/README.md#L21-L25)

Explicit global installs:

```bash
npx skills@latest add lencx/skills -a claude-code -g
npx skills@latest add lencx/skills -a codex -g
```

[README lines 27–35](https://github.com/lencx/skills/blob/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d/README.md#L27-L35)

### Codex native plugin

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add lencx/skills
codex plugin add lencx-skills@lencx
```

[README lines 37–44](https://github.com/lencx/skills/blob/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d/README.md#L37-L44)

The first command registers the GitHub repository as a marketplace; the second selects this repository’s named plugin.

### Claude Code native plugin

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add lencx/skills
claude plugin install lencx-skills@lencx
```

[README lines 46–51](https://github.com/lencx/skills/blob/3dc2694268d3e462738553cba094954d4df9412d/README.md#L46-L51)

No user-facing installation or download procedure is documented for `lencx-skills-codex.zip`. It is neither committed nor published as a release asset. Within the inspected scope, the script is build/distribution scaffolding rather than the active documented installation route.

## Custom or experimental aspects

- Nothing in the scoped files is explicitly labeled experimental.
- The Claude layout appears conventional: marketplace manifest, schema-backed plugin manifest, and repository-relative `skills/` declaration.
- The Codex `interface` block is platform-specific presentation metadata and lacks a schema reference, but the repository alone does not establish that it is experimental or nonstandard.
- The packaging shell script is plainly repository-specific/custom infrastructure.
- The unversioned ZIP filename, absence of release automation, absence of release assets, and lack of ZIP installation instructions make the archive path look unfinished or reserved for future/manual distribution.
- There is no evidence of a custom runtime, installer, hook, or loader: both native manifests expose the same ordinary checked-in `skills/` tree.

```text
1	# Adding vendor skills
2	
3	Vendor skills are third-party skills cherry-picked from upstream repos
4	into [`skills/vendor/`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/vendor).
5	The [`vendor.yaml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/vendor.yaml)
6	manifest tracks each upstream source plus the last-synced date and commit
7	SHA, so re-syncing is reproducible.
8	
9	## Quick add
10	
11	```bash
12	./scripts/add-vendor.sh owner/repo/path/to/skill
13	
14	# Examples
15	./scripts/add-vendor.sh marimo-team/skills/skills/marimo-notebook
16	./scripts/add-vendor.sh vercel-labs/agent-skills/skills/next-js
17	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --name my-name --branch dev owner/repo/skills/some-skill
18	
19	# Group into a series subdir
20	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --series fullstack-nextjs vercel/vercel-plugin/skills/nextjs
21	
22	# Or via Makefile
23	make add-vendor SOURCE=owner/repo/path/to/skill
24	
25	# GitHub URLs also work
26	./scripts/add-vendor.sh https://github.com/marimo-team/skills/tree/main/skills/marimo-notebook
27	```
28	
29	This verifies the upstream path exists, adds an entry to `vendor.yaml`, and
30	syncs the skill immediately. Pass `--no-sync` to only add the entry without
31	downloading.
32	
33	**Dependencies:** `gh` (GitHub CLI, authenticated) and `yq` (YAML processor).
34	
35	## Series grouping
36	
37	When you're vendoring a coherent set of skills around a single tech stack
38	(e.g. Next.js + Supabase + shadcn), pass `--series <name>` so the skills
39	land in `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/` instead of being flat. The
40	`series` field is recorded in `vendor.yaml` and honored by `sync-vendor.sh`.
41	
42	```yaml
43	# vendor.yaml
44	- name: nextjs
45	  series: fullstack-nextjs              # ← optional, omit for flat layout
46	  upstream:
47	    owner: vercel
48	    repo: vercel-plugin
49	    path: skills/nextjs
50	    branch: main
51	  last_sync: { date: "...", commit: "..." }
52	```
53	
54	This results in `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/nextjs/SKILL.md`. The
55	`npx skills@latest add` discovery does a 5-level fallback recursive
56	search, so series subdirs are still discovered.
57	
58	Existing flat entries (no `series` field) keep working unchanged. Active
59	series in this repo:
60	
61	- **`fullstack-nextjs`** — see [Skills overview > Fullstack Next.js series](../skills/index.md#fullstack-nextjs-series)
62	
63	## Manual config
64	
65	If you'd rather edit `vendor.yaml` by hand:
66	
67	```yaml
68	- name: my-skill
69	  upstream:
70	    owner: org-name
71	    repo: skills-repo
72	    path: skills/my-skill
73	    branch: main
74	  last_sync:
75	    date: ""
76	    commit: ""
77	```
78	
79	Then run `make sync` to download and stamp `last_sync`.
80	
81	## Check for upstream updates
82	
83	```bash
84	make sync-check
85	```
86	
87	This dry-runs the sync against the recorded `last_sync.commit` for each
88	entry and prints which skills have new commits upstream. Run `make sync`
89	to apply.
90	
91	## Why not just install upstream directly?
92	
93	`npx skills add owner/repo/path/to/skill` works one skill at a time and
94	leaves no manifest. Vendoring into this repo gives you:
95	
96	- A single install command for the whole curated set
97	  (`npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`).
98	- A pinned commit per skill so a reckless upstream change doesn't surprise you.
99	- A diff in your repo when you re-sync, which is your chance to read what
100	  changed before accepting it.
101	
102	## Don't edit vendored skills in place
103	
104	Modifications under `skills/vendor/` get overwritten by `make sync`. If you
105	need to customize a vendored skill, fork it into `skills/local/` and drop
106	the upstream entry from `vendor.yaml`. See [Conventions](../conventions.md).
107
```
</details></tool-use>

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# pre-push — run the catalog gates before anything leaves this machine.
3	#
4	# Installed by `make install-hooks` (symlinked to .git/hooks/pre-push).
5	# Mirrors .github/workflows/validate.yml, so CI failures show up here first.
6	#
7	# Bypass for a genuinely urgent push:  git push --no-verify
8	# Uninstall:                           rm .git/hooks/pre-push
9	
10	set -uo pipefail
11	
12	REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" || exit 1
13	cd "$REPO_ROOT" || exit 1
14	
15	LOG="$(mktemp -t agent-skills-prepush.XXXXXX)"
16	trap 'rm -f "$LOG"' EXIT
17	
18	printf 'pre-push: running make validate…\n' >&2
19	if make validate --no-print-directory >"$LOG" 2>&1; then
20	  printf 'pre-push: ok\n' >&2
21	  exit 0
22	fi
23	
24	printf '\npre-push: FAILED — push aborted:\n\n' >&2
25	tail -n 25 "$LOG" >&2
26	printf '\nRe-run in full with:  make validate\n(bypass with:         git push --no-verify)\n' >&2
27	exit 1
28
```

The repository has a working **cross-agent distribution path through `npx skills`** and a valid multi-category Claude marketplace manifest. Codex support relies on the portable `.agents/skills` convention rather than a separate Codex package.

Current status from read-only validation:

- `marketplace.json` validation passed: **61 declared skill roots**, no missing paths or duplicate catalog entries.
- `vendor.yaml` contains **40 vendored skill entries**.
- The full tree contains **63 `SKILL.md` files**, because two declared vendor roots contain nested `upstream/SKILL.md` files that the marketplace validator does not inventory.
- **15 skills** contain optional `agents/openai.yaml`; only one is locally authored.

## 1. Current user install path

The authoritative public command is:

```bash
npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
```

The trailing `/skills` is essential. Without it, the CLI searches the repository’s root `.agents/skills`, which is only a dogfooding symlink farm rather than the published collection. The README documents both the command and this warning at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/README.md:7-18`.

Flow:

1. `npx skills` parses `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` as the repository and `skills` as the subpath.
2. Its search root becomes `<repo>/skills`.
3. It reads `<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.
4. It discovers `skills/local/**/SKILL.md` and `skills/vendor/**/SKILL.md`, then uses the manifest to group the picker.
5. In a project install, canonical skill content goes into `.agents/skills/<name>`. Universal consumers such as Codex read that directly; Claude Code receives `.claude/skills/<name>` links.

The subpath resolution is explicitly documented at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md:24-52`, while target placement is described at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/docs/workflows/creating-local-skills.md:20-30`.

Because the interactive picker currently has a scrolling bug, the README also offers:

- `--yes` to install everything;
- `--list` to enumerate names;
- `--skill <name>` for one skill.

See `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/README.md:20-34`.

### Documentation contradiction

`CLAUDE.md`’s overview omits the required `/skills` suffix:

```text
npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills
```

at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/CLAUDE.md:5-9`, despite explaining the correct subpath later at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/CLAUDE.md:96-111`.

Because `AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `CLAUDE.md`, Codex sees the same incorrect overview command. The symlink contract is documented at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/skill-author/references/this-repo-conventions.md:128-131`.

## 2. Who consumes `marketplace.json`

| Consumer | How it uses the file |
|---|---|
| `npx skills` | Active, documented consumer. Uses `pluginRoot`, plugin names, sources, and skill paths to group the installer picker. |
| Claude Code plugin UI | Understands the complete marketplace schema, including descriptions, categories, tags, versions, and `strict`, once the marketplace is registered. |
| Codex | Does **not** read it natively. Codex reads the installed `.agents/skills` tree and optional per-skill `agents/openai.yaml`. |
| Cursor/OpenCode/etc. | Likewise do not consume the Claude marketplace natively; `npx skills` bridges into their target directories. |

The field-by-field consumer table is at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md:90-103`. Cross-agent behavior and the fact that Codex does not natively read the manifest are stated at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md:261-281`.

Operationally, this repository documents only the `npx skills` route. It does not document a repository-specific native command such as `claude plugin marketplace add ...`, nor does CI test such registration.

## 3. Claude plugin structure completeness

### What is complete

`skills/.claude-plugin/` contains one `marketplace.json`. For this multi-category collection, that is intentional and sufficient: `plugin.json` is for a single-plugin repository and is not required here. See:

- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md:10-22`
- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md:249-259`

The manifest has:

- marketplace name and owner;
- metadata description and version;
- 16 inline plugin groups;
- `source: "./"` and `strict: false` for each group;
- explicit skill directories.

Representative structure is at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json:1-24`; the complete group list spans lines 11-233.

The read-only validator passed all 61 declared roots. Its implemented checks are JSON parsing, reserved exact names, directory/SKILL existence, duplicate paths, and an on-disk coverage warning: `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/scripts/validate-marketplace.sh:35-124`.

### What remains incomplete

1. **Native Claude marketplace installation is not documented or smoke-tested.**  
   The nested manifest location is thoroughly justified for `npx skills`, but there is no demonstrated native Claude registration flow for this repository. Therefore the structure is proven for npx grouping, not end-to-end native `/plugin` installation.

2. **Marketplace version is permanently set to `1.0.0`.**  
   The repository’s own documentation says that when `metadata.version` is present, users only see updates when it changes, yet the manifest remains at `1.0.0`:  
   `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json:7-10` and `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md:238-247`.  
   There is no release target or CI gate enforcing a bump.

3. **Validation is not a full Claude marketplace schema check.**  
   It does not validate owner shape, semver, unique plugin names, `source` containment, field types, tags/categories, or the documented prohibition on names that merely impersonate official marketplaces. It checks only an exact reserved-name array at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/scripts/validate-marketplace.sh:46-67`.

4. **README catalog inventory is stale.**  
   It says there are seven groups and lists an older subset at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/README.md:73-80`; the current manifest has 16 groups through `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json:11-233`.

5. **The fixed manifest coverage check misses nested skills.**  
   `validate-marketplace.sh` inventories only `find -maxdepth 4` at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/scripts/validate-marketplace.sh:98-113`. Two vendor bundles contain deeper skill manifests:

   - `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/nextjs/upstream/SKILL.md:1-5`
   - `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/react-best-practices/upstream/SKILL.md:1-8`

   Under the repository’s documented recursive-to-five discovery model, these may be installer-visible and fall into **Other**, even though validation reports complete coverage. This needs an actual `npx skills --list` smoke assertion or explicit exclusion policy.

## 4. Vendor and CI validation

### Existing vendor machinery

`vendor.yaml` records name, upstream owner/repository/path/branch, and last-sync timestamp/SHA; see its representative entry at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/vendor.yaml:1-12`.

`add-vendor.sh`:

- verifies the upstream GitHub path;
- rejects duplicate names;
- appends to `vendor.yaml`;
- optionally downloads immediately.

See `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/scripts/add-vendor.sh:146-190`.

`sync-vendor.sh` supports a remote freshness check and frozen entries, then downloads upstream trees and updates `last_sync`: `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/scripts/sync-vendor.sh:122-187`.

### Validation gaps

1. **There is no `vendor.yaml` validator.**  
   `make validate` runs only frontmatter parsing, marketplace validation, and TODO validation: `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/Makefile:28-33`. It does not check:

   - YAML/schema validity for `vendor.yaml`;
   - unique upstream sources;
   - safe `name` or `series` values;
   - vendor entry ↔ on-disk directory correspondence;
   - vendor entry ↔ marketplace correspondence;
   - required `last_sync` fields;
   - valid `frozen` or `renamed_from` structure.

2. **`vendor.yaml` changes trigger CI but CI never reads it.**  
   The workflow includes `vendor.yaml` in path filters at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/.github/workflows/validate.yml:11-28`, but its steps only lint SKILL frontmatter, validate the marketplace, and validate TODO format at lines 44-56.

3. **`sync-check` is not a publish gate.**  
   It is only a standalone Make target at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/Makefile:3-7`; neither `make validate` nor CI runs it.

4. **“Pinned/reproducible” is overstated.**  
   Documentation says each vendored skill is pinned by commit at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/docs/workflows/adding-vendor-skills.md:91-100`, but synchronization downloads `git/trees/$branch`, not the recorded SHA, at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/scripts/sync-vendor.sh:69-95`. The SHA is used as a freshness marker and written after download at lines 182-185; it is not an immutable fetch reference.

5. **Adding a vendor does not update its marketplace category.**  
   That remains a manual second step in `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/CLAUDE.md:106-111`. Because unlisted skills are warning-only, a newly synced vendor can pass publishing gates while silently entering **Other**: `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/scripts/validate-marketplace.sh:98-124`.

6. **No end-to-end install test exists in CI.**  
   A clean-project install is documented as a manual test at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/docs/workflows/creating-local-skills.md:89-98`, but the workflow never invokes `npx skills --list` or installs into a scratch project.

## 5. Codex packaging status and concrete gaps

### Current support

Codex packaging is based on the portable Agent Skills shape:

- canonical `SKILL.md` with `name` and `description`;
- project/global installation under `.agents/skills`;
- optional `agents/openai.yaml`;
- root `AGENTS.md` for repository instructions.

The portability contract and Codex behavior are documented at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/docs/reference/agent-skill-compatibility.md:7-17` and lines 32-41.

There is no `.codex/` package directory, but that is not inherently missing: this repository explicitly treats `.agents/skills` as the universal Codex discovery directory. A `.codex` path appears only in agent-artifact secret-scrubbing scope at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/.pre-commit-hooks.yaml:21-31`.

### Concrete Codex gaps

1. **No direct Codex install section or Codex-native catalog.**  
   Users must infer that the generic npx command installs for Codex. `marketplace.json` groups are unavailable inside Codex because Codex does not consume that file natively.

2. **Codex hard limits are not enforced by CI.**  
   The repo targets 64-character names and 1024-character descriptions, and records a real Codex skip incident at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/docs/reference/agent-skill-compatibility.md:43-64`.  
   `lint-skill.sh` enforces those limits at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh:177-230`, but `make validate` and CI run only `lint-frontmatter.sh`, whose checks stop at parseability and string types: `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh:19-27`. A future overlong skill can therefore pass publishing CI and be skipped by Codex.

3. **Optional `agents/openai.yaml` coverage is sparse and unvalidated.**  
   Only 15 of 61 declared skills have it; 14 are inherited from the engineering-fundamentals vendor series, and the only local example is Clash Proxy API: `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/clash-proxy-api/agents/openai.yaml:1-4`.  
   This metadata is optional, so missing files do not prevent loading, but most skills lack Codex display metadata, default prompts, and invocation policy.

4. **The scaffolder does not create Codex metadata.**  
   It creates only the skill root plus `references`, `scripts`, `assets`, and `SKILL.md`: `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh:399-412`. There is no `agents/openai.yaml` template or optional scaffolding flag.

5. **No OpenAI metadata validation exists.**  
   Neither Makefile nor CI checks `agents/openai.yaml` schema, prompt references, short-description length, or invocation-policy values.

6. **Repository-clone discovery is intentionally partial.**  
   Root `.agents/skills` contains only a small dogfooding subset, not the 61 distributed skills. This is explicitly intentional and separate from distribution at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/CLAUDE.md:127-142`, but it means opening the cloned repository directly in Codex is not equivalent to installing the collection.

## Recommended priority

1. Correct the missing `/skills` suffix in `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`.
2. Resolve or explicitly exclude the two nested `upstream/SKILL.md` files and make marketplace coverage use the same discovery semantics as `npx skills`.
3. Add a CI install/list smoke test that asserts the expected skill set and Codex `.agents/skills` destination.
4. Run portable 64/1024 validation across every published skill in CI.
5. Add a `vendor.yaml` schema/tree/catalog consistency validator.
6. Decide whether `agents/openai.yaml` should remain opt-in or receive a template and validator.
7. Document and test native Claude marketplace registration, plus automate marketplace version discipline.
8. Generate or validate README category counts from `marketplace.json` to prevent further drift.

No files were modified.
